L.skv: ^149:4^ Quia beneplácitum est Dómino in pópulo suo: * et exaltábit mansuétos in salútem.

L.skp: ^149:1^ Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: * let his praise be in the church of the saints.
L.skq: ^149:2^ Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: * and let the children of Sion be joyful in their king.
L.skt: ^149:3^ Let them praise his name in choir: * let them sing to him with the timbrel and the psaltery.
L.sku: ^149:4^ For the Lord is well pleased with his people: * and he will exalt the meek unto salvation.
L.skx: ^149:5^ The saints shall rejoice in glory: * they shall be joyful in their beds.
L.skz: ^149:6^ The high praises of God shall be in their mouth: * and two-edged swords in their hands:
L.sl1: ^149:7^ To execute vengeance upon the nations, * chastisements among the people:
L.sl3: ^149:8^ To bind their kings with fetters, * and their nobles with manacles of iron.
L.sl4: ^149:9^ To execute upon them the judgment that is written: * this glory is to all his saints.

L.18nz: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

L.13o4: ^℣.^ Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.
L.jl0: ^℟.^ That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
L.p85: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
L.13ks: ^℣.^ May the divine assistance ^✠^ remain with us always.
L.7sb: ^118:1^ ^(Aleph)^ Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.
L.7sd: ^118:2^ Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia ejus: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
L.7sg: ^118:3^ Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis ejus ambulavérunt.
L.7sk: ^118:4^ Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
L.7t6: ^118:5^ Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas justificatiónes tuas!
L.7ti: ^118:6^ Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
L.7tj: ^118:7^ Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici judícia justítiæ tuæ.
L.7tm: ^118:8^ Justificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
L.7tt: ^118:9^ ^(Beth)^ In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
L.7qv: ^118:10^ In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
L.7r3: ^118:11^ In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
L.7r5: ^118:12^ Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me justificatiónes tuas.
L.7r7: ^118:13^ In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia judícia oris tui.
L.7rk: ^118:14^ In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.
L.7s6: ^118:15^ In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.
L.7sa: ^118:16^ In justificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.
L.7sc: ^118:1^ ^(Aleph)^ Blessed are the undefiled in the way, * who walk in the law of the Lord.
L.7se: ^118:2^ Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.
L.7sf: ^118:3^ For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.
L.7sj: ^118:4^ Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.
L.7t5: ^118:5^ O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.
L.7th: ^118:6^ Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.
L.7tk: ^118:7^ I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.
L.7tl: ^118:8^ I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.
L.7tu: ^118:9^ ^(Béth)^ By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.
L.7qw: ^118:10^ With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.
L.7r4: ^118:11^ Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.
L.7r6: ^118:12^ Blessed art thou, O Lord: * teach me thy justifications.
L.7r8: ^118:13^ With my lips * I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth.
L.7rj: ^118:14^ I have been delighted in the way of thy testimonies, * as in all riches.
L.7s5: ^118:15^ I will meditate on thy commandments: * and I will consider thy ways.
L.7s9: ^118:16^ I will think of thy justifications: * I will not forget thy words.
L.mxc: Dómine Deus omnípotens, qui ad princípium hujus diéi nos perveníre fecísti: tua nos hódie salva virtúte; ut in hac die ad nullum declinémus peccátum, sed semper ad tuam justítiam faciéndam nostra procédant elóquia, dirigántur cogitatiónes et ópera.
L.p77: O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who has safely brought us to the beginning of this day: defend us by thy mighty power; and grant that this day we fall into no sin, but that all our doings may be ordered by thy governance, to do always what is righteous in thy sight.
L.q2t: Sancta María et omnes Sancti intercédant pro nobis ad Dóminum, ut nos mereámur ab eo adjuvári et salvári, qui vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.
L.13o7: ^℣.^ Precious in the sight of the Lord
L.12kk: ^℟.^ Is the death of his saints.
L.nlz: Holy Mary and all the Saints, intercede for us with the Lord, our God, so that we may merit His help and salvation, who lives and reigns for ever and ever.
L.oez: Kýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
L.13q9: ^℣.^ Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.
L.12di: ^℟.^ Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
L.mut: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
L.13m3: ^℣.^ O God, come to my assistance;
L.oiw: Lord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
L.13k6: ^℣.^ Look upon thy servants and upon thy works: and direct their children.
L.1234: ^℟.^ And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us. Direct thou the works of our hands; yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.
L.p5t: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.
L.105p: ^Benedictio.^ Dóminus nos benedícat, ^✠^ et ab omni malo deféndat, et ad vitam perdúcat ætérnam. Et fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
L.13nl: ^℣.^ Our help is ^✠^ in the name of the Lord,
L.105x: ^Benediction.^ May the Lord bless us, ^✠^ protect us from all evil and bring us to everlasting life. And may the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

L.7si: ^118:49^ ^(Zai)^ Memor esto verbi tui servo tuo, * in quo mihi spem dedísti.
L.7sl: ^118:50^ Hæc me consoláta est in humilitáte mea: * quia elóquium tuum vivificávit me.
L.7sn: ^118:51^ Supérbi iníque agébant usquequáque: * a lege autem tua non declinávi.
L.7sq: ^118:52^ Memor fui judiciórum tuórum a sǽculo, Dómine: * et consolátus sum.
L.7ss: ^118:53^ Deféctio ténuit me, * pro peccatóribus derelinquéntibus legem tuam.
L.7st: ^118:54^ Cantábiles mihi erant justificatiónes tuæ, * in loco peregrinatiónis meæ.
L.7sw: ^118:55^ Memor fui nocte nóminis tui, Dómine: * et custodívi legem tuam.
L.7sx: ^118:56^ Hæc facta est mihi: * quia justificatiónes tuas exquisívi.
L.7t0: ^118:57^ ^(Heth)^ Pórtio mea, Dómine, * dixi custodíre legem tuam.
L.7t1: ^118:58^ Deprecátus sum fáciem tuam in toto corde meo: * miserére mei secúndum elóquium tuum.
L.7t3: ^118:59^ Cogitávi vias meas: * et convérti pedes meos in testimónia tua.
L.7t8: ^118:60^ Parátus sum, et non sum turbátus: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
L.7t9: ^118:61^ Funes peccatórum circumpléxi sunt me: * et legem tuam non sum oblítus.
L.7tc: ^118:62^ Média nocte surgébam ad confiténdum tibi, * super judícia justificatiónis tuæ.
L.7te: ^118:63^ Párticeps ego sum ómnium timéntium te: * et custodiéntium mandáta tua.
L.7tf: ^118:64^ Misericórdia tua, Dómine, plena est terra: * justificatiónes tuas doce me.
L.7sh: ^118:49^ ^(Zai)^ Be thou mindful of thy word to thy servant, * in which thou hast given me hope.
L.7sm: ^118:50^ This hath comforted me in my humiliation: * because thy word hath enlivened me.
L.7so: ^118:51^ The proud did iniquitously altogether: * but I declined not from thy law.
L.7sp: ^118:52^ I remembered, O Lord, thy judgments of old: * and I was comforted.
L.7sr: ^118:53^ A fainting hath taken hold of me, * because of the wicked that forsake thy law.
L.7su: ^118:54^ Thy justifications were the subject of my song, * in the place of my pilgrimage.
L.7sv: ^118:55^ In the night I have remembered thy name, O Lord: * and have kept thy law.
L.7sy: ^118:56^ This happened to me: * because I sought after thy justifications.
L.7sz: ^118:57^ ^(Heth)^ O Lord, my portion, * I have said, I would keep thy law.
L.7t2: ^118:58^ I entreated thy face with all my heart: * have mercy on me according to thy word.
L.7t4: ^118:59^ I have thought on my ways: * and turned my feet unto thy testimonies.
L.7t7: ^118:60^ I am ready, and am not troubled: * that I may keep thy commandments.
L.7ta: ^118:61^ The cords of the wicked have encompassed me: * but I have not forgotten thy law.
L.7tb: ^118:62^ I rose at midnight to give praise to thee; * for the judgments of thy justification.
L.7td: ^118:63^ I am a partaker with all them that fear thee, * and that keep thy commandments.
L.7tg: ^118:64^ The earth, O Lord, is full of thy mercy: * teach me thy justifications.
L.7to: ^118:97^ ^(Mem)^ Quómodo diléxi legem tuam, Dómine? * tota die meditátio mea est.
L.7tp: ^118:98^ Super inimícos meos prudéntem me fecísti mandáto tuo: * quia in ætérnum mihi est.
L.7ts: ^118:99^ Super omnes docéntes me intelléxi: * quia testimónia tua meditátio mea est.
L.7qc: ^118:100^ Super senes intelléxi: * quia mandáta tua quæsívi.
L.7qd: ^118:101^ Ab omni via mala prohíbui pedes meos: * ut custódiam verba tua.
L.7qf: ^118:102^ A judíciis tuis non declinávi: * quia tu legem posuísti mihi.
L.7qi: ^118:103^ Quam dúlcia fáucibus meis elóquia tua, * super mel ori meo!
L.7qj: ^118:104^ A mandátis tuis intelléxi: * proptérea odívi omnem viam iniquitátis.
L.7ql: ^118:105^ ^(Nun)^ Lucérna pédibus meis verbum tuum, * et lumen sémitis meis.
L.7qo: ^118:106^ Jurávi, et státui * custodíre judícia justítiæ tuæ.
L.7qp: ^118:107^ Humiliátus sum usquequáque, Dómine: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
L.7qs: ^118:108^ Voluntária oris mei beneplácita fac, Dómine: * et judícia tua doce me.
L.7qu: ^118:109^ Ánima mea in mánibus meis semper: * et legem tuam non sum oblítus.
L.7qx: ^118:110^ Posuérunt peccatóres láqueum mihi: * et de mandátis tuis non errávi.
L.7qz: ^118:111^ Hereditáte acquisívi testimónia tua in ætérnum: * quia exsultátio cordis mei sunt.
L.7r2: ^118:112^ Inclinávi cor meum ad faciéndas justificatiónes tuas in ætérnum, * propter retributiónem.
L.7tn: ^118:97^ ^(Mem)^ How have I loved thy law, O Lord! * it is my meditation all the day.
L.7tq: ^118:98^ Through thy commandment, thou hast made me wiser than my enemies: * for it is ever with me.
L.7tr: ^118:99^ I have understood more than all my teachers: * because thy testimonies are my meditation.
L.7qb: ^118:100^ I have had understanding above ancients: * because I have sought thy commandments.
L.7qe: ^118:101^ I have restrained my feet from every evil way: * that I may keep thy words.
L.7qg: ^118:102^ I have not declined from thy judgments, * because thou hast set me a law.
L.7qh: ^118:103^ How sweet are thy words to my palate! * more than honey to my mouth.
L.7qk: ^118:104^ By thy commandments I have had understanding: * therefore have I hated every way of iniquity.
L.7qm: ^118:105^ ^(Nun)^ Thy word is a lamp to my feet, * and a light to my paths.
L.7qn: ^118:106^ I have sworn and am determined * to keep the judgments of thy justice.
L.7qq: ^118:107^ I have been humbled, O Lord, exceedingly: * quicken thou me according to thy word.
L.7qr: ^118:108^ The free offerings of my mouth make acceptable, O Lord: * and teach me thy judgments.
L.7qt: ^118:109^ My soul is continually in my hands: * and I have not forgotten thy law.
L.7qy: ^118:110^ Sinners have laid a snare for me: * but I have not erred from thy precepts.
L.7r0: ^118:111^ I have purchased thy testimonies for an inheritance for ever: * because they are the joy of my heart.
L.7r1: ^118:112^ I have inclined my heart to do thy justifications for ever, * for the reward.
L.14cx: ear us, O Father, gracious and forgiving,
L.lru: And thou, O Christ, the co-eternal Word,
L.ra0: Who, with the Holy Ghost, by all things living
L.p2m: Now and to endless ages art adored.
L.7r9: ^118:145^ ^(Coph)^ Clamávi in toto corde meo, exáudi me, Dómine: * justificatiónes tuas requíram.
L.7rb: ^118:146^ Clamávi ad te, salvum me fac: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
L.7re: ^118:147^ Prævéni in maturitáte, et clamávi: * quia in verba tua supersperávi.
L.7rg: ^118:148^ Prævenérunt óculi mei ad te dilúculo: * ut meditárer elóquia tua.
L.7ri: ^118:149^ Vocem meam audi secúndum misericórdiam tuam, Dómine: * et secúndum judícium tuum vivífica me.
L.7rl: ^118:150^ Appropinquavérunt persequéntes me iniquitáti: * a lege autem tua longe facti sunt.
L.7rn: ^118:151^ Prope es tu, Dómine: * et omnes viæ tuæ véritas.
L.7rq: ^118:152^ Inítio cognóvi de testimóniis tuis: * quia in ætérnum fundásti ea.
L.7rs: ^118:153^ ^(Res)^ Vide humilitátem meam, et éripe me: * quia legem tuam non sum oblítus.
L.7ru: ^118:154^ Júdica judícium meum, et rédime me: * propter elóquium tuum vivífica me.
L.7rv: ^118:155^ Longe a peccatóribus salus: * quia justificatiónes tuas non exquisiérunt.
L.7ry: ^118:156^ Misericórdiæ tuæ multæ, Dómine: * secúndum judícium tuum vivífica me.
L.7s0: ^118:157^ Multi qui persequúntur me, et tríbulant me: * a testimóniis tuis non declinávi.
L.7s2: ^118:158^ Vidi prævaricántes, et tabescébam: * quia elóquia tua non custodiérunt.
L.7s4: ^118:159^ Vide quóniam mandáta tua diléxi, Dómine: * in misericórdia tua vivífica me.
L.7s7: ^118:160^ Princípium verbórum tuórum, véritas: * in ætérnum ómnia judícia justítiæ tuæ.
L.7ra: ^118:145^ ^(Coph)^ I cried with my whole heart, hear me, O Lord: * I will seek thy justifications.
L.7rc: ^118:146^ I cried unto thee, save me: * that I may keep thy commandments.
L.7rd: ^118:147^ I prevented the dawning of the day, and cried: * because in thy words I very much hoped.
L.7rf: ^118:148^ My eyes to thee have prevented the morning: * that I might meditate on thy words.
L.7rh: ^118:149^ Hear thou my voice, O Lord, according to thy mercy: * and quicken me according to thy judgment.
L.7rm: ^118:150^ They that persecute me have drawn nigh to iniquity; * but they are gone far off from thy law.
L.7ro: ^118:151^ Thou art near, O Lord: * and all thy ways are truth.
L.7rp: ^118:152^ I have known from the beginning concerning thy testimonies: * that thou hast founded them for ever.
L.7rr: ^118:153^ ^(Res)^ See my humiliation and deliver me: * for I have not forgotten thy law.
L.7rt: ^118:154^ Judge my judgment and redeem me: * quicken thou me for thy word’s sake.
L.7rw: ^118:155^ Salvation is far from sinners; * because they have not sought thy justifications.
L.7rx: ^118:156^ Many, O Lord, are thy mercies: * quicken me according to thy judgment.
L.7rz: ^118:157^ Many are they that persecute me, and afflict me; * but I have not declined from thy testimonies.
L.7s1: ^118:158^ I beheld the transgressors, and I pined away; * because they kept not thy word.
L.7s3: ^118:159^ Behold I have loved thy commandments, O Lord; * quicken me thou in thy mercy.
L.7s8: ^118:160^ The beginning of thy words is truth: * all the judgments of thy justice are for ever.

L.nd3: Glory be to God on high, and on earth peace to men of good will. We praise Thee. We bless Thee. We adore Thee. We glorify Thee. We give Thee thanks for Thy great glory. O Lord God, heavenly King, God the Father almighty. O Lord Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son. O Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father. Who takest away the sins of the world, have mercy on us. Who takest away the sins of the world, receive our prayer. Who sittest at the right hand of the Father, have mercy on us. For Thou only art holy. Thou only art the Lord. L.10rn: ^Deinde ad medium Altaris extendens, elevans et jungens manus, dicit, si dicendum est, Credo in unum Deum, et prosequitur junctis manibus. Cum dicit Deum, caput Cruci inclinat: quod similiter facit, cum dicit Jesum Christum, et simul adorátur. Ad illa autem verba Et incarnátus est, genuflectit usque dum dicatur Et homo factus est. In fine ad Et vitam ventúri sæculi, signat se signo crucis a fronte ad pectus.^
L.mgr: Credo in unum Deum, Patrem omnipoténtem, factórem cæli et terræ, visibílium ómnium et invisibílium. Et in unum Dóminum Jesum Christum, Fílium Dei unigénitum. Et ex Patre natum ante ómnia sǽcula. Deum de Deo, Lumen de Lúmine, Deum verum de Deo vero. Génitum, non factum, consubstantiálem Patri: per quem ómnia facta sunt. Qui propter nos hómines et propter nostram salútem descéndit de cælis. ^Hic genuflectitur^ Et incarnátus est de Spíritu Sancto ex María Vírgine: Et homo factus est. Crucifíxus étiam pro nobis: sub Póntio Piláto passus, et sepúltus est. Et resurréxit tértia die, secúndum Scriptúras. Et ascéndit in cælum: sedet ad déxteram Patris. Et íterum ventúrus est cum glória judicáre vivos et mórtuos: cujus regni non erit finis. Et in Spíritum Sanctum, Dóminum et vivificántem: qui ex Patre Filióque procédit. Qui cum Patre et Fílio simul adorátur et conglorificátur: qui locútus est per Prophétas. Et unam sanctam cathólicam et apostólicam Ecclésiam. Confíteor unum baptísma in remissiónem peccatórum. Et exspécto resurrectiónem mortuórum. Et vitam ventúri sæculi. Amen.
L.11ex: ^On Sundays and certain Feasts the priest recites the Creed, a summary of the Catholic Doctrine. This profession of faith was drawn up in the General Councils of Nicaea in 325 and Constantinople in 381 to condemn heretics who denied that Jesus Christ and the Holy Ghost were God.^
L.nq0: I believe in one God, the Father almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things, visible and invisible.
L.lqp: And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God. And born of the Father, before all ages. God of God: Light of Light: true God of true God. Begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father, by whom all things were made. Who, for us men, and for our salvation, came down from heaven. ^Here kneel down.^ And became incarnate by the Holy Ghost of the Virgin Mary: and was made man. He was crucified also for us, suffered under Pontius Pilate, and was buried. And the third day He rose again according to the Scriptures. And ascended into heaven, and sitteth at the right hand of the Father. And He shall come again with glory to judge both the living and the dead, of whose kingdom there shall be no end.
L.lqq: And in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Giver of Life, proceeding from the Father and the Son. Who together, with the Father and the Son, is adored and glorified: Who spoke by the prophets. And in one, holy, Catholic and Apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins. And I look for the resurrection of the dead. And the life of the world to come. Amen.

L.r1l: Vere dignum et justum est, æquum et salutáre, nos tibi semper et ubíque grátias ágere: Dómine sancte, Pater omnípotens, ætérne Deus: Qui cum unigénito Fílio tuo et Spíritu Sancto unus es Deus, unus es Dóminus: non in uníus singularitáte persónæ, sed in uníus Trinitáte substántiæ. Quod enim de tua glória, revelánte te, crédimus, hoc de Fílio tuo, hoc de Spíritu Sancto sine differéntia discretiónis sentímus. Ut in confessióne veræ sempiternǽque Deitátis, et in persónis propríetas, et in esséntia únitas, et in majestáte adorétur æquálitas. Quam laudant Angeli atque Archángeli, Chérubim quoque ac Séraphim: qui non cessant clamáre quotídie, una voce dicéntes:
L.o6f: It is truly meet and just, right and for our salvation, that we should at all times, and in all places, give thanks unto Thee, O holy Lord, Father almighty, everlasting God; Who, together with Thine only-begotten Son, and the Holy Ghost, art one God, one Lord: not in the oneness of a single Person, but in the Trinity of one substance. For what we believe by Thy revelation of Thy glory, the same do we believe of Thy Son, the same of the Holy Ghost, without difference or separation. So that in confessing the true and everlasting Godhead, distinction in persons, unity in essence, and equality in majesty may be adored. Which the Angels and Archangels, the Cherubim also and Seraphim do praise: who cease not daily to cry out, with one voice saying:

L.qz1: Unde et mémores, Dómine, nos servi tui, sed et plebs tua sancta, ejúsdem Christi Fílii tui, Dómini nostri, tam beátæ passiónis, nec non et ab ínferis resurrectiónis, sed et in cælos gloriósæ ascensiónis: offérimus præcláræ majestáti tuæ de tuis donis ac datis, ^Jungit manus, et signat ter super Hostiam, et Calicem simul, dicens:^ Hóstiam ^✠^ puram, Hóstiam ^✠^ sanctam, Hóstiam ^✠^ immaculátam, ^Signat semel super Hostiam, dicens:^ Panem ^✠^ sanctum vitæ ætérnæ, ^et semel super Calicem, dicens:^ et Cálicem ^✠^ salútis perpétuæ.

L.r9c: Wherefore, O Lord, we Thy servants, as also Thy holy people, calling to mind the blessed Passion of the same Christ, Thy Son, our Lord, and also His Resurrection from the dead and His glorious Ascension into heaven: do offer unto Thy most excellent Majesty of Thine own gifts, bestowed upon us, ^He joins his hands and signs thrice the Host and Chalice with the Sign of the Cross.^ a pure ^✠^ Host, a holy ^✠^ Host, an unspotted ^✠^ Host, ^He signs the Host and the Chalice, with the Sign of the Cross.^ the holy ^✠^ Bread of eternal life, and the Chalice ^✠^ of everlasting salvation.

L.r0b: Upon which vouchsafe to look with a propitious and serene countenance, and to accept them, as Thou wert graciously pleased to accept the gifts of Thy just servant Abel, and the sacrifice of our patriarch Abraham, and that which Thy high priest Melchisedech offered to Thee, a holy sacrifice, an unspotted victim.

L.mxf: Dómine Jesu Christe, qui dixísti Apóstolis tuis: Pacem relínquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis: ne respícias peccáta mea, sed fidem Ecclésiæ tuæ; eámque secúndum voluntátem tuam pacificáre et coadunáre dignéris: Qui vivis et regnas Deus per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
L.11zw: ^With his hands joined and resting on the altar, standing inclined, he says the three following prayers:^
L.p5s: O Lord Jesus Christ, who saidst to Thine Apostles: Peace I leave you, My peace I give you: regard not my sins, but the faith of Thy Church; and vouchsafe to grant her that peace and unity which is agreeable to Thy will: Who livest and reignest God, world without end. Amen.
L.mxe: Dómine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi, qui ex voluntáte Patris, cooperánte Spíritu Sancto, per mortem tuam mundum vivificásti: líbera me per hoc sacrosánctum Corpus et Sánguinem tuum ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis, et univérsis malis: et fac me tuis semper inhærére mandátis, et a te numquam separári permíttas: Qui cum eódem Deo Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas Deus in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
L.p5r: O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, who, according to the will of Thy Father, with the cooperation of the Holy Ghost, hast by Thy death given life to the world; deliver me by this Thy most sacred Body and Blood, from all my iniquities and from all evils; and make me always cleave to Thy commandments, and suffer me never to be separated from Thee, Who livest and reignest, with the same God the Father and the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.
L.794: Percéptio Córporis tui, Dómine Jesu Christe, quod ego indígnus súmere præsúmo, non mihi provéniat in judícium et condemnatiónem: sed pro tua pietáte prosit mihi ad tutaméntum mentis et córporis, et ad medélam percipiéndam: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
L.ogw: Let not the partaking of Thy Body, O Lord, Jesus Christ, which I, though unworthy, presume to receive, turn to my judgment and condemnation; but let it, through Thy mercy, become a safeguard and remedy, both for soul and body; Who with God the Father, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, livest and reignest God, world without end. Amen.

L.r1o: Vere dignum et justum est, æquum et salutáre, nos tibi semper et ubíque grátias ágere: Dómine sancte, Pater omnípotens, ætérne Deus: per Christum, Dóminum nostrum. Per quem majestátem tuam laudant Angeli, adórant Dominatiónes, tremunt Potestátes. Cæli cælorúmque Virtútes ac beáta Séraphim sócia exsultatióne concélebrant. Cum quibus et nostras voces ut admítti jubeas, deprecámur, súpplici confessione dicéntes:
L.o63: It is truly meet and just, and profitable unto salvation, that we should at all times, and in all places, give thanks to Thee, O Holy Lord, Father Almighty, eternal God, through Christ, our Lord. Through whom the Angels praise Thy Majesty, the Dominions adore it, the Powers are in awe. Which the heavens and the hosts of heaven together with the blessed Seraphim joyfully do magnify. And do Thou command that it be permitted us to join with them in confessing Thee, while we say with lowly praise:
L.742: In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. Hoc erat in princípio apud Deum. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt: et sine ipso factum est nihil, quod factum est: in ipso vita erat, et vita erat lux hóminum: et lux in ténebris lucet, et ténebræ eam non comprehendérunt.
L.724: Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Joánnes. Hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine, ut omnes créderent per illum. Non erat ille lux, sed ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine.
L.70t: Erat lux vera, quæ illúminat omnem hóminem veniéntem in hunc mundum. In mundo erat, et mundus per ipsum factus est, et mundus eum non cognóvit. In própria venit, et sui eum non recepérunt. Quotquot autem recepérunt eum, dedit eis potestátem fílios Dei fíeri, his, qui credunt in nómine ejus: qui non ex sanguínibus, neque ex voluntáte carnis, neque ex voluntáte viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt. ^Genuflectit dicens:^ Et Verbum caro factum est, ^Et surgens prosequitur:^ et habitávit in nobis: et vídimus glóriam ejus, glóriam quasi Unigéniti a Patre, plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
L.7bc: The beginning ^+^ of the holy Gospel according to John
L.746: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by Him, and without Him was made nothing that was made: in Him was life, and the life was the Light of men; and the Light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to testify concerning the Light, that all might believe through Him. He was not the Light, but he was to testify concerning the Light. That was the true Light, which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world. He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not. He came unto His own, and His own received Him not. But as many as received Him to them He gave power to become sons of God, to them that believe in His Name, who are born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. ^Here all kneel.^ And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: and we saw His glory, the glory as of the Only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

L.8ge: ^38:2^ Dixi: Custódiam vias meas: * ut non delínquam in lingua mea.
L.8gh: ^38:2^ Pósui ori meo custódiam, * cum consísteret peccátor advérsum me.
L.8gj: ^38:3^ Obmútui, et humiliátus sum, et sílui a bonis: * et dolor meus renovátus est.
L.8gk: ^38:4^ Concáluit cor meum intra me: * et in meditatióne mea exardéscet ignis.
L.8gp: ^38:5^ Locútus sum in lingua mea: * Notum fac mihi, Dómine, finem meum.
L.8gn: ^38:5^ Et númerum diérum meórum quis est: * ut sciam quid desit mihi.
L.8gs: ^38:6^ Ecce mensurábiles posuísti dies meos: * et substántia mea tamquam níhilum ante te.
L.8gt: ^38:6^ Verúmtamen univérsa vánitas, * omnis homo vivens.
L.8gx: ^38:7^ Verúmtamen in imágine pertránsit homo: * sed et frustra conturbátur.
L.8gw: ^38:7^ Thesaurízat: * et ignórat cui congregábit ea.
L.8gz: ^38:8^ Et nunc quæ est exspectátio mea? Nonne Dóminus? * Et substántia mea apud te est.
L.8h0: ^38:9^ Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me: * oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me.
L.8g3: ^38:10^ Obmútui, et non apérui os meum, quóniam tu fecísti: * ámove a me plagas tuas.
L.8g4: ^38:12^ A fortitúdine manus tuæ ego deféci in increpatiónibus: * propter iniquitátem corripuísti hóminem.
L.8g6: ^38:12^ Et tabéscere fecísti sicut aráneam ánimam ejus: * verúmtamen vane conturbátur omnis homo.
L.8g9: ^38:13^ Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe lácrimas meas.
L.8gb: ^38:13^ Ne síleas: quóniam ádvena ego sum apud te, et peregrínus, * sicut omnes patres mei.
L.8gd: ^38:14^ Remítte mihi, ut refrígerer priúsquam ábeam, * et ámplius non ero.
L.8gg: ^38:2^ I said: I will take heed to my ways: * that I sin not with my tongue.
L.8gf: ^38:2^ I have set guard to my mouth, * when the sinner stood against me.
L.8gi: ^38:3^ I was dumb, and was humbled, and kept silence from good things: * and my sorrow was renewed.
L.8gl: ^38:4^ My heart grew hot within me: * and in my meditation a fire shall flame out.
L.8go: ^38:5^ I spoke with my tongue: * O Lord, make me know my end.
L.8gm: ^38:5^ And what is the number of my days: * that I may know what is wanting to me.
L.8gr: ^38:6^ Behold thou hast made my days measurable: * and my substance is as nothing before thee.
L.8gq: ^38:6^ And indeed all things are vanity: * every man living.
L.8gv: ^38:7^ Surely man passeth as an image: * yea, and he is disquieted in vain.
L.8gu: ^38:7^ He storeth up: * and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things.
L.8gy: ^38:8^ And now what is my hope? Is it not the Lord? * And my substance is with thee.
L.8h1: ^38:9^ Deliver thou me from all my iniquities: * thou hast made me a reproach to the fool.
L.8g2: ^38:10^ I was dumb, and I opened not my mouth, because thou hast done it: * remove thy scourges from me.
L.8g7: ^38:12^ The strength of thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes: * thou hast corrected man for iniquity.
L.8g5: ^38:12^ And thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider: * surely in vain is any man disquieted.
L.8ga: ^38:13^ Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication: * give ear to my tears.
L.8g8: ^38:13^ Be not silent: for I am a stranger with thee, * and a sojourner as all my fathers were.
L.8gc: ^38:14^ O forgive me, that I may be refreshed, before I go hence, * and be no more.
L.zxh: ^Ant.^ Ut non delínquam in lingua mea.
L.zim: ^Ant.^ That I sin not with my tongue.
L.8hz: ^40:2^ Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
L.8i1: ^40:3^ Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum ejus.
L.8i3: ^40:4^ Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris ejus: * univérsum stratum ejus versásti in infirmitáte ejus.
L.8i5: ^40:5^ Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
L.8i7: ^40:6^ Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
L.8ib: ^40:7^ Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor ejus congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
L.8ia: ^40:7^ Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
L.8id: ^40:8^ Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
L.8ig: ^40:9^ Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
L.8hq: ^40:10^ Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
L.8hs: ^40:11^ Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
L.8hu: ^40:12^ In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
L.8hw: ^40:13^ Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
L.8hx: ^40:14^ Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
L.8i0: ^40:2^ Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.
L.8i2: ^40:3^ The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.
L.8i4: ^40:4^ The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.
L.8i6: ^40:5^ I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.
L.8i8: ^40:6^ My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?
L.8i9: ^40:7^ And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.
L.8ic: ^40:7^ He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.
L.8ie: ^40:8^ All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.
L.8if: ^40:9^ They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?
L.8hp: ^40:10^ For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.
L.8hr: ^40:11^ But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.
L.8ht: ^40:12^ By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.
L.8hv: ^40:13^ But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.
L.8hy: ^40:14^ Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.
L.zcq: ^Ant.^ Sana Dómine ánimam meam, qui peccávi tibi.
L.ycn: ^Ant.^ Heal my soul, O Lord, for I have sinned against Thee.
L.8jh: ^43:2^ Deus áuribus nostris audívimus: * patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
L.8ji: ^43:2^ Opus, quod operátus es in diébus eórum, * et in diébus antíquis.
L.8jl: ^43:3^ Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos: * afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
L.8jp: ^43:4^ Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, * et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos:
L.8jq: ^43:4^ Sed déxtera tua, et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui: * quóniam complacuísti in eis.
L.8js: ^43:5^ Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus: * qui mandas salútes Jacob.
L.8jt: ^43:6^ In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu: * et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
L.8jw: ^43:7^ Non enim in arcu meo sperábo: * et gládius meus non salvábit me.
L.8jy: ^43:8^ Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos: * et odiéntes nos confudísti.
L.8jz: ^43:9^ In Deo laudábimur tota die: * et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
L.8ii: ^43:10^ Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos: * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
L.8ij: ^43:11^ Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros: * et qui odérunt nos, diripiébant sibi.
L.8il: ^43:12^ Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum: * et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
L.8io: ^43:13^ Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio: * et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
L.8ip: ^43:14^ Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, * subsannatiónem et derísum his, qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
L.8ir: ^43:15^ Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus: * commotiónem cápitis in pópulis.
L.8iu: ^43:16^ Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, * et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
L.8iv: ^43:17^ A voce exprobrántis, et obloquéntis: * a fácie inimíci, et persequéntis.
L.8iy: ^43:18^ Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos, nec oblíti sumus te: * et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
L.8j0: ^43:19^ Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum: * et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua:
L.8j2: ^43:20^ Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, * et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
L.8j4: ^43:21^ Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, * et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
L.8j6: ^43:22^ Nonne Deus requíret ista? * ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
L.8j7: ^43:22^ Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die: * æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
L.8ja: ^43:23^ Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? * exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
L.8jb: ^43:24^ Quare fáciem tuam avértis, * oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ, et tribulatiónis nostræ?
L.8je: ^43:25^ Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra: * conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
L.8jg: ^43:26^ Exsúrge, Dómine, ádjuva nos: * et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
L.8jk: ^43:2^ We have heard, O God, with our ears: * our fathers have declared to us,
L.8jj: ^43:2^ The work thou hast wrought in their days, * and in the days of old.
L.8jm: ^43:3^ Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: * thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.
L.8jo: ^43:4^ For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: * neither did their own arm save them.
L.8jn: ^43:4^ But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: * because thou wast pleased with them.
L.8jr: ^43:5^ Thou art thyself my king and my God, * who commandest the saving of Jacob.
L.8ju: ^43:6^ Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: * and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.
L.8jv: ^43:7^ For I will not trust in my bow: * neither shall my sword save me.
L.8jx: ^43:8^ But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: * and hast put them to shame that hate us.
L.8k0: ^43:9^ In God shall we glory all the day long: * and in thy name we will give praise for ever.
L.8ih: ^43:10^ But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: * and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.
L.8ik: ^43:11^ Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: * and they that hated us plundered for themselves.
L.8im: ^43:12^ Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: * thou hast scattered us among the nations.
L.8in: ^43:13^ Thou hast sold thy people for no price: * and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.
L.8iq: ^43:14^ Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, * a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.
L.8is: ^43:15^ Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: * a shaking of the head among the people.
L.8it: ^43:16^ All the day long my shame is before me: * and the confusion of my face hath covered me.
L.8iw: ^43:17^ At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: * at the face of the enemy and persecutor.
L.8ix: ^43:18^ All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: * and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.
L.8iz: ^43:19^ And our heart hath not turned back: * neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.
L.8j1: ^43:20^ For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: * and the shadow of death hath covered us.
L.8j3: ^43:21^ If we have forgotten the name of our God, * and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:
L.8j8: ^43:22^ Shall not God search out these things: * for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.
L.8j5: ^43:22^ Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: * we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
