L.8d4: ^35:3^ Quóniam dolóse egit in conspéctu ejus: * ut inveniátur iníquitas ejus ad ódium.
L.8d6: ^35:4^ Verba oris ejus iníquitas, et dolus: * nóluit intellégere ut bene ágeret.
L.8d8: ^35:5^ Iniquitátem meditátus est in cubíli suo: * ástitit omni viæ non bonæ, malítiam autem non odívit.
L.8d9: ^35:6^ Dómine, in cælo misericórdia tua: * et véritas tua usque ad nubes.
L.8dc: ^35:7^ Justítia tua sicut montes Dei: * judícia tua abýssus multa.
L.8db: ^35:7^ Hómines, et juménta salvábis, Dómine: * quemádmodum multiplicásti misericórdiam tuam, Deus.
L.8dg: ^35:8^ Fílii autem hóminum, * in tégmine alárum tuárum sperábunt.
L.8dh: ^35:9^ Inebriabúntur ab ubertáte domus tuæ: * et torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis eos.
L.8cu: ^35:10^ Quóniam apud te est fons vitæ: * et in lúmine tuo vidébimus lumen.
L.8cw: ^35:11^ Præténde misericórdiam tuam sciéntibus te, * et justítiam tuam his, qui recto sunt corde.
L.8cy: ^35:12^ Non véniat mihi pes supérbiæ: * et manus peccatóris non móveat me.
L.8cz: ^35:13^ Ibi cecidérunt qui operántur iniquitátem: * expúlsi sunt, nec potuérunt stare.
L.8d2: ^35:2^ The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin: * there is no fear of God before his eyes.
L.8d3: ^35:3^ For in his sight he hath done deceitfully, * that his iniquity may be found unto hatred.
L.8d5: ^35:4^ The words of his mouth are iniquity and guile: * he would not understand that he might do well.
L.8d7: ^35:5^ He hath devised iniquity on his bed, * he hath set himself on every way that is not good: but evil he hath not hated.
L.8da: ^35:6^ O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, * and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.
L.8de: ^35:7^ Thy justice is as the mountains of God, * thy judgments are a great deep.
L.8dd: ^35:7^ Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord: * O how hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God!
L.8df: ^35:8^ But the children of men * shall put their trust under the covert of thy wings.
L.8di: ^35:9^ They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house; * and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure.
L.8ct: ^35:10^ For with thee is the fountain of life; * and in thy light we shall see light.
L.8cv: ^35:11^ Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, * and thy justice to them that are right in heart.
L.8cx: ^35:12^ Let not the foot of pride come to me, * and let not the hand of the sinner move me.
L.8d0: ^35:13^ There the workers of iniquity are fallen, * they are cast out, and could not stand.
L.y8b: ^Ant.^ Fight against them that fight against me.
L.8e9: ^36:1^ Noli æmulári in malignántibus: * neque zeláveris faciéntes iniquitátem.
L.8ex: ^36:2^ Quóniam tamquam fænum velóciter aréscent: * et quemádmodum ólera herbárum cito décident.
L.8fi: ^36:3^ Spera in Dómino, et fac bonitátem: * et inhábita terram, et pascéris in divítiis ejus.
L.8fm: ^36:4^ Delectáre in Dómino: * et dabit tibi petitiónes cordis tui.
L.8fp: ^36:5^ Revéla Dómino viam tuam, et spera in eo: * et ipse fáciet.
L.8fr: ^36:6^ Et edúcet quasi lumen justítiam tuam: et judícium tuum tamquam merídiem: * súbditus esto Dómino, et ora eum.
L.8ft: ^36:7^ Noli æmulári in eo, qui prosperátur in via sua: * in hómine faciénte injustítias.
L.8fv: ^36:8^ Désine ab ira, et derelínque furórem: * noli æmulári ut malignéris.
L.8fx: ^36:9^ Quóniam qui malignántur, exterminabúntur: * sustinéntes autem Dóminum, ipsi hereditábunt terram.
L.8dm: ^36:10^ Et adhuc pusíllum, et non erit peccátor: * et quæres locum ejus et non invénies.
L.8dp: ^36:11^ Mansuéti autem hereditábunt terram: * et delectabúntur in multitúdine pacis.
L.8dq: ^36:12^ Observábit peccátor justum: * et stridébit super eum déntibus suis.
L.8dt: ^36:13^ Dóminus autem irridébit eum: * quóniam próspicit quod véniet dies ejus.
L.8du: ^36:14^ Gládium evaginavérunt peccatóres: * intendérunt arcum suum,
L.8dx: ^36:14^ Ut deíciant páuperem et ínopem: * ut trucídent rectos corde.
L.8dy: ^36:15^ Gládius eórum intret in corda ipsórum: * et arcus eórum confringátur.
L.8e1: ^36:16^ Mélius est módicum justo, * super divítias peccatórum multas.
L.8e3: ^36:17^ Quóniam brácchia peccatórum conteréntur: * confírmat autem justos Dóminus.
L.8e4: ^36:18^ Novit Dóminus dies immaculatórum: * et heréditas eórum in ætérnum erit.
L.8e6: ^36:19^ Non confundéntur in témpore malo, et in diébus famis saturabúntur: * quia peccatóres períbunt.
L.8eb: ^36:20^ Inimíci vero Dómini mox ut honorificáti fúerint et exaltáti: * deficiéntes, quemádmodum fumus defícient.
L.8ec: ^36:21^ Mutuábitur peccátor, et non solvet: * justus autem miserétur et tríbuet.
L.8ef: ^36:22^ Quia benedicéntes ei hereditábunt terram: * maledicéntes autem ei disperíbunt.
L.8eg: ^36:23^ Apud Dóminum gressus hóminis dirigéntur: * et viam ejus volet.
L.8ei: ^36:24^ Cum cecíderit non collidétur: * quia Dóminus suppónit manum suam.
L.8el: ^36:25^ Júnior fui, étenim sénui: * et non vidi justum derelíctum, nec semen ejus quærens panem.
L.8en: ^36:26^ Tota die miserétur et cómmodat: * et semen illíus in benedictióne erit.
L.8ep: ^36:27^ Declína a malo, et fac bonum: * et inhábita in sǽculum sǽculi.
L.8es: ^36:28^ Quia Dóminus amat judícium, et non derelínquet sanctos suos: * in ætérnum conservabúntur.
L.8er: ^36:28^ Injústi puniéntur: * et semen impiórum períbit.
L.8ev: ^36:29^ Justi autem hereditábunt terram: * et inhabitábunt in sǽculum sǽculi super eam.
L.8ey: ^36:30^ Os justi meditábitur sapiéntiam, * et lingua ejus loquétur judícium.
L.8f0: ^36:31^ Lex Dei ejus in corde ipsíus, * et non supplantabúntur gressus ejus.
L.8f2: ^36:32^ Consíderat peccátor justum: * et quærit mortificáre eum.
L.8f5: ^36:33^ Dóminus autem non derelínquet eum in mánibus ejus: * nec damnábit eum, cum judicábitur illi.
L.8f7: ^36:34^ Exspécta Dóminum, et custódi viam ejus: et exaltábit te ut hereditáte cápias terram: * cum períerint peccatóres vidébis.
L.8f9: ^36:35^ Vidi ímpium superexaltátum, * et elevátum sicut cedros Líbani.
L.8fb: ^36:36^ Et transívi, et ecce non erat: * et quæsívi eum, et non est invéntus locus ejus.
L.8fc: ^36:37^ Custódi innocéntiam, et vide æquitátem: * quóniam sunt relíquiæ hómini pacífico.
L.8ff: ^36:38^ Injústi autem disperíbunt simul: * relíquiæ impiórum interíbunt.
L.8fh: ^36:39^ Salus autem justórum a Dómino: * et protéctor eórum in témpore tribulatiónis.
L.8fl: ^36:40^ Et adjuvábit eos Dóminus et liberábit eos: * et éruet eos a peccatóribus, et salvábit eos: quia speravérunt in eo.
L.8e8: ^36:1^ Be not emulous of evildoers; * nor envy them that work iniquity.
L.8ew: ^36:2^ For they shall shortly wither away as grass, * and as the green herbs shall quickly fall.
L.8fj: ^36:3^ Trust in the Lord, and do good, * and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with its riches.
L.8fn: ^36:4^ Delight in the Lord, * and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.
L.8fo: ^36:5^ Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, * and he will do it.
L.8fq: ^36:6^ And he will bring forth thy justice as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday: * be subject to the Lord and pray to him.
L.8fs: ^36:7^ Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; * the man who doth unjust things.
L.8fu: ^36:8^ Cease from anger, and leave rage; * have no emulation to do evil.
L.8fw: ^36:9^ For the evildoers shall be cut off: * but they that wait upon the Lord shall inherit the land.
L.8dn: ^36:10^ For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: * and thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it.
L.8do: ^36:11^ But the meek shall inherit the land, * and shall delight in abundance of peace.
L.8dr: ^36:12^ The sinner shall watch the just man: * and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.
L.8ds: ^36:13^ But the Lord shall laugh at him: * for he foreseeth that his day shall come.
L.8dv: ^36:14^ The wicked have drawn out the sword: * they have bent their bow.
L.8dw: ^36:14^ To cast down the poor and needy, * to kill the upright of heart.
L.8dz: ^36:15^ Let their sword enter into their own hearts, * and let their bow be broken.
L.8e0: ^36:16^ Better is a little to the just, * than the great riches of the wicked.
L.8e2: ^36:17^ For the arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; * but the Lord strengtheneth the just.
L.8e5: ^36:18^ The Lord knoweth the days of the undefiled; * and their inheritance shall be for ever.
L.8e7: ^36:19^ They shall not be confounded in the evil time; and in the days of famine they shall be filled, * because the wicked shall perish.
L.8ea: ^36:20^ And the enemies of the Lord, presently after they shall be honoured and exalted, * shall come to nothing and vanish like smoke.
L.8ed: ^36:21^ The sinner shall borrow, and not pay again; * but the just sheweth mercy and shall give.
L.8ee: ^36:22^ For such as bless him shall inherit the land: * but such as curse him shall perish.
L.8eh: ^36:23^ With the Lord shall the steps of a man be directed, * and he shall like well his way.
L.8ej: ^36:24^ When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, * for the Lord putteth his hand under him.
L.8ek: ^36:25^ I have been young, and now am old; * and I have not seen the just forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread.
L.8em: ^36:26^ He sheweth mercy, and lendeth all the day long; * and his seed shall be in blessing.
L.8eo: ^36:27^ Decline from evil and do good, * and dwell for ever and ever.
L.8eq: ^36:28^ For the Lord loveth judgment, and will not forsake his saints: * they shall be preserved for ever.
L.8et: ^36:28^ The unjust shall be punished, * and the seed of the wicked shall perish.
L.8eu: ^36:29^ But the just shall inherit the land, * and shall dwell therein for evermore.
L.8ez: ^36:30^ The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: * and his tongue shall speak judgment.
L.8f1: ^36:31^ The law of his God is in his heart, * and his steps shall not be supplanted.
L.8f3: ^36:32^ The wicked watcheth the just man, * and seeketh to put him to death.
L.8f4: ^36:33^ But the Lord will not leave him in his hands; * nor condemn him when he shall be judged.
L.8f6: ^36:34^ Expect the Lord and keep his way: and he will exalt thee to inherit the land: * when the sinners shall perish thou shalt see.
L.8f8: ^36:35^ I have seen the wicked highly exalted, * and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus.
L.8fa: ^36:36^ And I passed by, and lo, he was not: * and I sought him and his place was not found.
L.8fd: ^36:37^ Keep innocence, and behold justice: * for there are remnants for the peaceable man.
L.8fe: ^36:38^ But the unjust shall be destroyed together: * the remnants of the wicked shall perish.
L.8fg: ^36:39^ But the salvation of the just is from the Lord, * and he is their protector in the time of trouble.
L.8fk: ^36:40^ And the Lord will help them and deliver them: * and he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them, because they have hoped in him.
L.ze7: ^Ant.^ Show thy way unto the Lord.
L.12e5: ^℟.^ Et véritas tua usque ad nubes.
L.13vk: ^℣.^ Thy mercy, O Lord, is in the heavens.
L.124d: ^℟.^ And thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds.
L.8mx: ^50:3^ Miserére ^‡^ mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
L.vl4: ^50:3^ Have mercy on me, ^‡^ O God, * according to thy great mercy.
L.ybp: ^Ant.^ Have mercy on me, O God.
L.ycr: ^Ant.^ Hearken to my cry, O Lord.
L.8th: ^62:2^ Deus, Deus meus, * ^‡^ ad te de luce vígilo.
L.w06: ^62:2^ O God, my God, * ^‡^ to thee do I watch at break of day.
L.xzo: ^Ant.^ Deus deus meus ad te de luce vígilo.
L.yyy: ^Ant.^ O God, my God, to thee have I watched at break of day.
L.xvv: ^Ant.^ Convérsus est furor tuus Dómine, et consolátus es me.
L.ztv: ^Ant.^ Thou hast turned away thine anger.
L.ztu: ^Ant.^ Thou hast turned away thine anger and consoled me.
L.83a: ^148:1^ Laudáte ^‡^ Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
L.z72: ^Ant.^ Praise the Lord in the highest.
L.7pt: ^114:1^ Diléxi, quóniam exáudiet Dóminus * vocem oratiónis meæ.
L.7pw: ^114:2^ Quia inclinávit aurem suam mihi: * et in diébus meis invocábo.
L.7px: ^114:3^ Circumdedérunt me dolóres mortis: * et perícula inférni invenérunt me.
L.7q0: ^114:3^ Tribulatiónem et dolórem invéni: * et nomen Dómini invocávi.
L.7q1: ^114:4^ O Dómine, líbera ánimam meam: * miséricors Dóminus, et justus, et Deus noster miserétur.
L.7q3: ^114:6^ Custódiens párvulos Dóminus: * humiliátus sum, et liberávit me.
L.7q5: ^114:7^ Convértere, ánima mea, in réquiem tuam: * quia Dóminus benefécit tibi.
L.7q8: ^114:8^ Quia erípuit ánimam meam de morte: * óculos meos a lácrimis, pedes meos a lapsu.
L.7pu: ^114:1^ I have loved, because the Lord will hear * the voice of my prayer.
L.7pv: ^114:2^ Because he hath inclined his ear unto me: * and in my days I will call upon him.
L.7pz: ^114:3^ The sorrows of death have compassed me: * and the perils of hell have found me.
L.7py: ^114:3^ I met with trouble and sorrow: * and I called upon the name of the Lord.
L.7q2: ^114:4^ O Lord, deliver my soul. * The Lord is merciful and just, and our God sheweth mercy.
L.7q4: ^114:6^ The Lord is the keeper of little ones: * I was humbled, and he delivered me.
L.7q6: ^114:7^ Turn, O my soul, into thy rest: * for the Lord hath been bountiful to thee.
L.7q7: ^114:8^ For he hath delivered my soul from death: * my eyes from tears, my feet from falling.
L.7q9: ^114:9^ I will please the Lord * in the land of the living.
L.yh5: ^Ant.^ I will please the Lord in the land of the living.
L.rug: ^115:1^ Crédidi, ^‡^ propter quod locútus sum: * ego autem humiliátus sum nimis.
L.ruh: ^115:1^ I have believed, ^‡^ therefore have I spoken; * but I have been humbled exceedingly.
L.yfz: ^Ant.^ I have believed therefore have I spoken.
L.rui: ^116:1^ Laudáte ^‡^ Dóminum, omnes gentes: * laudáte eum, omnes pópuli:
L.z71: ^Ant.^ Praise the Lord all ye nations.
L.yfs: ^Ant.^ I cried to the Lord and he heard me.
L.7ub: ^120:1^ Levávi óculos meos in montes, * unde véniet auxílium mihi.
L.7uc: ^120:2^ Auxílium meum a Dómino, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
L.7uf: ^120:3^ Non det in commotiónem pedem tuum: * neque dormítet qui custódit te.
L.7uh: ^120:4^ Ecce, non dormitábit neque dórmiet, * qui custódit Israël.
L.7ui: ^120:5^ Dóminus custódit te, Dóminus protéctio tua, * super manum déxteram tuam.
L.7uk: ^120:6^ Per diem sol non uret te: * neque luna per noctem.
L.7um: ^120:7^ Dóminus custódit te ab omni malo: * custódiat ánimam tuam Dóminus.
L.7uo: ^120:8^ Dóminus custódiat intróitum tuum, et éxitum tuum: * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
L.7ua: ^120:1^ I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, * from whence help shall come to me.
L.7ud: ^120:2^ My help is from the Lord, * who made heaven and earth.
L.7ue: ^120:3^ May he not suffer thy foot to be moved: * neither let him slumber that keepeth thee.
L.7ug: ^120:4^ Behold he shall neither slumber nor sleep, * that keepeth Israel.
L.7uj: ^120:5^ The Lord is thy keeper, the Lord is thy protection * upon thy right hand.
L.7ul: ^120:6^ The sun shall not burn thee by day: * nor the moon by night.
L.7un: ^120:7^ The Lord keepeth thee from all evil: * may the Lord keep thy soul.
L.7up: ^120:8^ May the Lord keep thy coming in and thy going out; * from henceforth now and for ever.
L.zlt: ^Ant.^ The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.
L.n6e: Fidélis servus et prudens, quem constítuit dóminus super famíliam suam: ut det illis in témpore trítici mensúram.
L.qos: The faithful and prudent servant whom the master will set over his household to give them their ration of grain in due time.
L.y1i: ^Ant.^ Dómine Deus, in adjutórium meum inténde.
L.yrg: ^Ant.^ Make haste O Lord God, to deliver me.
L.y57: ^Ant.^ Esto mihi, Dómine, in Deum protectórem.
L.xo2: ^Ant.^ Be Thou my God my protector.
L.ztp: ^Ant.^ Thou hast redeemed the rod of Thine inheritance.
L.xki: ^Ant.^ And we will call upon Thy name, O Lord.
L.8um: ^77:1^ Atténdite, pópule meus, legem meam: * inclináte aurem vestram in verba oris mei.
L.8v9: ^77:2^ Apériam in parábolis os meum: * loquar propositiónes ab inítio.
L.8vy: ^77:3^ Quanta audívimus et cognóvimus ea: * et patres nostri narravérunt nobis.
L.8wl: ^77:4^ Non sunt occultáta a fíliis eórum: * in generatióne áltera.
L.8wk: ^77:4^ Narrántes laudes Dómini, et virtútes ejus: * et mirabília ejus, quæ fecit.
L.8xa: ^77:5^ Et suscitávit testimónium in Jacob: * et legem pósuit in Israël.
L.8xc: ^77:5^ Quanta mandávit pátribus nostris nota fácere ea fíliis suis: * ut cognóscat generátio áltera.
L.8xx: ^77:6^ Fílii qui nascéntur, et exsúrgent, * et narrábunt fíliis suis.
L.8y6: ^77:7^ Ut ponant in Deo spem suam, et non obliviscántur óperum Dei: * et mandáta ejus exquírant.
L.8y9: ^77:8^ Ne fiant sicut patres eórum: * generátio prava et exásperans.
L.8y8: ^77:8^ Generátio, quæ non diréxit cor suum: * et non est créditus cum Deo spíritus ejus.
L.8yb: ^77:9^ Fílii Ephrem intendéntes et mitténtes arcum: * convérsi sunt in die belli.
L.8u1: ^77:10^ Non custodiérunt testaméntum Dei: * et in lege ejus noluérunt ambuláre.
L.8u4: ^77:11^ Et oblíti sunt benefactórum ejus: * et mirabílium ejus quæ osténdit eis.
L.8u5: ^77:12^ Coram pátribus eórum fecit mirabília in terra Ægýpti: * in campo Táneos.
L.8u8: ^77:13^ Interrúpit mare, et perdúxit eos: * et státuit aquas quasi in utre.
L.8ua: ^77:14^ Et dedúxit eos in nube diéi: * et tota nocte in illuminatióne ignis.
L.8uc: ^77:15^ Interrúpit petram in erémo: * et adaquávit eos velut in abýsso multa.
L.8ud: ^77:16^ Et edúxit aquam de petra: * et dedúxit tamquam flúmina aquas.
L.8ug: ^77:17^ Et apposuérunt adhuc peccáre ei: * in iram excitavérunt Excélsum in inaquóso.
L.8ui: ^77:18^ Et tentavérunt Deum in córdibus suis, * ut péterent escas animábus suis.
L.8uk: ^77:19^ Et male locúti sunt de Deo: * dixérunt: Numquid póterit Deus paráre mensam in desérto?
L.8uq: ^77:20^ Quóniam percússit petram, et fluxérunt aquæ: * et torréntes inundavérunt.
L.8up: ^77:20^ Numquid et panem póterit dare, * aut paráre mensam pópulo suo?
L.8us: ^77:21^ Ídeo audívit Dóminus, et dístulit: * et ignis accénsus est in Jacob, et ira ascéndit in Israël.
L.8uu: ^77:22^ Quia non credidérunt in Deo: * nec speravérunt in salutári ejus:
L.8uw: ^77:23^ Et mandávit núbibus désuper: * et jánuas cæli apéruit.
L.8uy: ^77:24^ Et pluit illis manna ad manducándum: * et panem cæli dedit eis.
L.8v0: ^77:25^ Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, * cibária misit eis in abundántia.
L.8v2: ^77:26^ Tránstulit Austrum de cælo: * et indúxit in virtúte sua Áfricum.
L.8v4: ^77:27^ Et pluit super eos sicut púlverem carnes: * et sicut arénam maris volatília pennáta.
L.8v6: ^77:28^ Et cecidérunt in médio castrórum eórum: * circa tabernácula eórum.
L.8v7: ^77:29^ Et manducavérunt, et saturáti sunt nimis, et desidérium eórum áttulit eis: * non sunt fraudáti a desidério suo.
L.8vb: ^77:30^ Adhuc escæ eórum erant in ore ipsórum: * et ira Dei ascéndit super eos.
L.8ve: ^77:31^ Et occídit pingues eórum, * et eléctos Israël impedívit.
L.8vg: ^77:32^ In ómnibus his peccavérunt adhuc: * et non credidérunt in mirabílibus ejus.
L.8vi: ^77:33^ Et defecérunt in vanitáte dies eórum: * et anni eórum cum festinatióne.
L.8vj: ^77:34^ Cum occíderet eos, quærébant eum: * et revertebántur, et dilúculo veniébant ad eum.
L.8vm: ^77:35^ Et rememoráti sunt quia Deus adjútor est eórum: * et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est.
L.8vo: ^77:36^ Et dilexérunt eum in ore suo, * et lingua sua mentíti sunt ei.
L.8vq: ^77:37^ Cor autem eórum non erat rectum cum eo: * nec fidéles hábiti sunt in testaménto ejus.
L.8vu: ^77:38^ Ipse autem est miséricors, et propítius fiet peccátis eórum: * et non dispérdet eos.
L.8vt: ^77:38^ Et abundávit ut avérteret iram suam: * et non accéndit omnem iram suam:
L.8vw: ^77:39^ Et recordátus est quia caro sunt: * spíritus vadens et non rédiens.
L.8w0: ^77:40^ Quóties exacerbavérunt eum in desérto, * in iram concitavérunt eum in inaquóso?
L.8w2: ^77:41^ Et convérsi sunt, et tentavérunt Deum: * et Sanctum Israël exacerbavérunt.
L.8w3: ^77:42^ Non sunt recordáti manus ejus, * die qua redémit eos de manu tribulántis.
L.8w6: ^77:43^ Sicut pósuit in Ægýpto signa sua, * et prodígia sua in campo Táneos.
L.8w8: ^77:44^ Et convértit in sánguinem flúmina eórum: * et imbres eórum, ne bíberent.
L.8wa: ^77:45^ Misit in eos cœnomyíam, et comédit eos: * et ranam, et dispérdidit eos.
L.8wc: ^77:46^ Et dedit ærúgini fructus eórum: * et labóres eórum locústæ.
L.8we: ^77:47^ Et occídit in grándine víneas eórum: * et moros eórum in pruína.
L.8wg: ^77:48^ Et trádidit grándini juménta eórum: * et possessiónem eórum igni.
L.8wi: ^77:49^ Misit in eos iram indignatiónis suæ: * indignatiónem, et iram, et tribulatiónem: immissiónes per ángelos malos.
L.8wo: ^77:50^ Viam fecit sémitæ iræ suæ, non pepércit a morte animábus eórum: * et juménta eórum in morte conclúsit.
L.8wq: ^77:51^ Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra Ægýpti: * primítias omnis labóris eórum in tabernáculis Cham.
L.8ws: ^77:52^ Et ábstulit sicut oves pópulum suum: * et perdúxit eos tamquam gregem in desérto.
L.8wu: ^77:53^ Et dedúxit eos in spe, et non timuérunt: * et inimícos eórum opéruit mare.
L.8wy: ^77:54^ Et indúxit eos in montem sanctificatiónis suæ: * montem, quem acquisívit déxtera ejus.
L.8wx: ^77:54^ Et ejécit a fácie eórum gentes: * et sorte divísit eis terram in funículo distributiónis.
L.8x0: ^77:55^ Et habitáre fecit in tabernáculis eórum: * tribus Israël.
L.8x1: ^77:56^ Et tentavérunt, et exacerbavérunt Deum excélsum: * et testimónia ejus non custodiérunt.
L.8x4: ^77:57^ Et avertérunt se, et non servavérunt pactum: * quemádmodum patres eórum convérsi sunt in arcum pravum.
L.8x5: ^77:58^ In iram concitavérunt eum in cóllibus suis: * et in sculptílibus suis ad æmulatiónem eum provocavérunt.
L.8x7: ^77:59^ Audívit Deus, et sprevit: * et ad níhilum redégit valde Israël.
L.8xe: ^77:60^ Et répulit tabernáculum Silo: * tabernáculum suum, ubi habitávit in homínibus.
L.8xg: ^77:61^ Et trádidit in captivitátem virtútem eórum: * et pulchritúdinem eórum in manus inimíci.
L.8xi: ^77:62^ Et conclúsit in gládio pópulum suum: * et hereditátem suam sprevit.
L.8xk: ^77:63^ Júvenes eórum comédit ignis: * et vírgines eórum non sunt lamentátæ.
L.8xl: ^77:64^ Sacerdótes eórum in gládio cecidérunt: * et víduæ eórum non plorabántur.
L.8xo: ^77:65^ Et excitátus est tamquam dórmiens Dóminus: * tamquam potens crapulátus a vino.
L.8xq: ^77:66^ Et percússit inimícos suos in posterióra: * oppróbrium sempitérnum dedit illis.
L.8xs: ^77:67^ Et répulit tabernáculum Joseph: * et tribum Éphraim non elégit.
L.8xu: ^77:68^ Sed elégit tribum Juda, * montem Sion quem diléxit.
L.8xw: ^77:69^ Et ædificávit sicut unicórnium sanctifícium suum in terra, * quam fundávit in sǽcula.
L.8y0: ^77:70^ Et elégit David, servum suum, et sústulit eum de grégibus óvium: * de post fœtántes accépit eum,
L.8y1: ^77:71^ Páscere Jacob, servum suum, * et Israël, hereditátem suam:
L.8y4: ^77:72^ Et pavit eos in innocéntia cordis sui: * et in intelléctibus mánuum suárum dedúxit eos.
L.zvw: ^Ant.^ Tu es Deus qui facis mirabília.
L.8ul: ^77:1^ Attend, O my people, to my law: * incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
L.8va: ^77:2^ I will open my mouth in parables: * I will utter propositions from the beginning.
L.8vx: ^77:3^ How great things have we heard and known, * and our fathers have told us.
L.8wm: ^77:4^ They have not been hidden from their children, * in another generation.
L.8wj: ^77:4^ Declaring the praises of the Lord, and his powers, * and his wonders which he hath done.
L.8x9: ^77:5^ And he set up a testimony in Jacob: * and made a law in Israel.
L.8xb: ^77:5^ How great things he commanded our fathers, that they should make the same known to their children: * that another generation might know them.
L.8xy: ^77:6^ The children that should be born and should rise up, * and declare them to their children.
L.8y5: ^77:7^ That they may put their hope in God and may not forget the works of God: * and may seek his commandments.
L.8ya: ^77:8^ That they may not become like their fathers, * a perverse and exasperating generation.
L.8y7: ^77:8^ A generation that set not their heart aright: * and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
L.8yc: ^77:9^ The sons of Ephraim who bend and shoot with the bow: * they have turned back in the day of battle.
L.8u2: ^77:10^ They kept not the covenant of God: * and in his law they would not walk.
L.8u3: ^77:11^ And they forgot his benefits, * and his wonders that he had shewn them.
L.8u6: ^77:12^ Wonderful things did he do in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, * in the field of Tanis.
L.8u7: ^77:13^ He divided the sea and brought them through: * and he made the waters to stand as in a vessel.
L.8u9: ^77:14^ And he conducted them with a cloud by day: * and all the night with a light of fire.
L.8ub: ^77:15^ He struck the rock in the wilderness: * and gave them to drink, as out of the great deep.
L.8ue: ^77:16^ He brought forth water out of the rock: * and made streams run down as rivers.
L.8uf: ^77:17^ And they added yet more sin against him: * they provoked the most High to wrath in the place without water.
L.8uh: ^77:18^ And they tempted God in their hearts, * by asking meat for their desires.
L.8uj: ^77:19^ And they spoke ill of God: * they said: Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?
L.8un: ^77:20^ Because he struck the rock, and the waters gushed out, * and the streams overflowed.
L.8uo: ^77:20^ Can he also give bread, * or provide a table for his people?
L.8ur: ^77:21^ Therefore the Lord heard, and was angry: * and a fire was kindled against Jacob, and wrath came up against Israel.
L.8ut: ^77:22^ Because they believed not in God: * and trusted not in his salvation.
L.8uv: ^77:23^ And he had commanded the clouds from above, * and had opened the doors of heaven.
L.8ux: ^77:24^ And had rained down manna upon them to eat, * and had given them the bread of heaven.
L.8uz: ^77:25^ Man ate the bread of angels: * he sent them provisions in abundance.
L.8v1: ^77:26^ He removed the south wind from heaven: * and by his power brought in the southwest wind.
L.8v3: ^77:27^ And he rained upon them flesh as dust: * and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea.
L.8v5: ^77:28^ And they fell in the midst of their camp, * round about their pavilions.
L.8v8: ^77:29^ So they did eat, and were filled exceedingly, and he gave them their desire: * they were not defrauded of that which they craved.
L.8vc: ^77:30^ As yet their meat was in their mouth: * and the wrath of God came upon them.
L.8vd: ^77:31^ And he slew the fat ones amongst them, * and brought down the chosen men of Israel.
L.8vf: ^77:32^ In all these things they sinned still: * and they believed not for his wondrous works.
L.8vh: ^77:33^ And their days were consumed in vanity, * and their years in haste.
L.8vk: ^77:34^ When he slew them, then they sought him: * and they returned, and came to him early in the morning.
L.8vl: ^77:35^ And they remembered that God was their helper: * and the most high God their redeemer.
L.8vn: ^77:36^ And they loved him with their mouth: * and with their tongue they lied unto him:
L.8vp: ^77:37^ But their heart was not right with him: * nor were they counted faithful in his covenant.
L.8vs: ^77:38^ But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins: * and will not destroy them.
L.8vr: ^77:38^ And many a time did he turn away his anger: * and did not kindle all his wrath.
L.8vv: ^77:39^ And he remembered that they are flesh: * a wind that goeth and returneth not.
L.8vz: ^77:40^ How often did they provoke him in the desert: * and move him to wrath in the place without water?
L.8w1: ^77:41^ And they turned back and tempted God: * and grieved the holy one of Israel.
L.8w4: ^77:42^ They remembered not his hand, * in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them:
L.8w5: ^77:43^ How he wrought his signs in Egypt, * and his wonders in the field of Tanis.
L.8w7: ^77:44^ And he turned their rivers into blood, * and their showers that they might not drink.
L.8w9: ^77:45^ He sent amongst them diverse sorts of flies, which devoured them: * and frogs which destroyed them.
L.8wb: ^77:46^ And he gave up their fruits to the blast, * and their labours to the locust.
L.8wd: ^77:47^ And he destroyed their vineyards with hail, * and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost.
L.8wf: ^77:48^ And he gave up their cattle to the hail, * and their stock to the fire.
L.8wh: ^77:49^ And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: * indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels.
L.8wn: ^77:50^ He made a way for a path to his anger: * he spared not their souls from death, and their cattle he shut up in death.
L.8wp: ^77:51^ And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt: * the firstfruits of all their labour in the tabernacles of Cham.
L.8wr: ^77:52^ And he took away his own people as sheep: * and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
L.8wt: ^77:53^ And he brought them out in hope, and they feared not: * and the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
L.8wv: ^77:54^ And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary: * the mountain which his right hand had purchased.
L.8ww: ^77:54^ And he cast out the Gentiles before them: * and by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution.
L.8wz: ^77:55^ And he made the tribes of Israel * to dwell in their tabernacles.
L.8x2: ^77:56^ Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God: * and they kept not his testimonies.
L.8x3: ^77:57^ And they turned away, and kept not the covenant: * even like their fathers they were turned aside as a crooked bow.
L.8x6: ^77:58^ They provoked him to anger on their hills: * and moved him to jealousy with their graven things.
L.8x8: ^77:59^ God heard, and despised them, * and he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing.
L.8xd: ^77:60^ And he put away the tabernacle of Silo, * his tabernacle where he dwelt among men.
L.8xf: ^77:61^ And he delivered their strength into captivity: * and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.
L.8xh: ^77:62^ And he shut up his people under the sword: * and he despised his inheritance.
L.8xj: ^77:63^ Fire consumed their young men: * and their maidens were not lamented.
L.8xm: ^77:64^ Their priests fell by the sword: * and their widows did not mourn.
L.8xn: ^77:65^ And the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep, * and like a mighty man that hath been surfeited with wine.
L.8xp: ^77:66^ And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts: * he put them to an everlasting reproach.
L.8xr: ^77:67^ And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph: * and chose not the tribe of Ephraim:
L.8xt: ^77:68^ But he chose the tribe of Juda, * mount Sion which he loved.
L.8xv: ^77:69^ And he built his sanctuary as of unicorns, in the land * which he founded for ever.
L.8xz: ^77:70^ And he chose his servant David, and took him from the flocks of sheep: * he brought him from following the ewes great with young,
L.8y2: ^77:71^ To feed Jacob his servant, * and Israel his inheritance.
L.8y3: ^77:72^ And he fed them in the innocence of his heart: * and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands.
L.ztg: ^Ant.^ Thou art the God That doest wonders.
L.8yp: ^78:1^ Deus, venérunt gentes in hereditátem tuam, polluérunt templum sanctum tuum: * posuérunt Jerúsalem in pomórum custódiam.
L.8yr: ^78:2^ Posuérunt morticína servórum tuórum, escas volatílibus cæli: * carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.
L.8yt: ^78:3^ Effudérunt sánguinem eórum tamquam aquam in circúitu Jerúsalem: * et non erat qui sepelíret.
L.8yv: ^78:4^ Facti sumus oppróbrium vicínis nostris: * subsannátio et illúsio his, qui in circúitu nostro sunt.
L.8yy: ^78:5^ Úsquequo, Dómine, irascéris in finem: * accendétur velut ignis zelus tuus?
L.8yz: ^78:6^ Effúnde iram tuam in gentes, quæ te non novérunt: * et in regna quæ nomen tuum non invocavérunt:
L.8z2: ^78:7^ Quia comedérunt Jacob: * et locum ejus desolavérunt.
L.8z3: ^78:8^ Ne memíneris iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum, cito antícipent nos misericórdiæ tuæ: * quia páuperes facti sumus nimis.
L.8z6: ^78:9^ Ádjuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos: * et propítius esto peccátis nostris, propter nomen tuum:
L.8yf: ^78:10^ Ne forte dicant in géntibus: Ubi est Deus eórum? * et innotéscat in natiónibus coram óculis nostris.
L.8yg: ^78:10^ Últio sánguinis servórum tuórum, qui effúsus est: * intróeat in conspéctu tuo gémitus compeditórum.
L.8yi: ^78:11^ Secúndum magnitúdinem brácchii tui, * pósside fílios mortificatórum.
L.8yk: ^78:12^ Et redde vicínis nostris séptuplum in sinu eórum: * impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi, Dómine.
L.8yn: ^78:13^ Nos autem pópulus tuus, et oves páscuæ tuæ, * confitébimur tibi in sǽculum.
L.8ym: ^78:13^ In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábimus laudem tuam.
L.8yq: ^78:1^ O God, the heathens are come into thy inheritance, they have defiled thy holy temple: * they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit.
L.8ys: ^78:2^ They have given the dead bodies of thy servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: * the flesh of thy saints for the beasts of the earth.
L.8yu: ^78:3^ They have poured out their blood as water, round about Jerusalem, * and there was none to bury them.
L.8yw: ^78:4^ We are become a reproach to our neighbours: * a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.
L.8yx: ^78:5^ How long, O Lord, wilt thou be angry for ever: * shall thy zeal be kindled like a fire?
L.8z0: ^78:6^ Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that have not known thee: * and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.
L.8z1: ^78:7^ Because they have devoured Jacob; * and have laid waste his place.
L.8z4: ^78:8^ Remember not our former iniquities: let thy mercies speedily prevent us, * for we are become exceeding poor.
L.8z5: ^78:9^ Help us, O God, our saviour: and for the glory of thy name, O Lord, deliver us: * and forgive us our sins for thy name’s sake:
L.8ye: ^78:10^ Lest they should say among the Gentiles: Where is their God? * And let him be made known among the nations before our eyes,
L.8yd: ^78:10^ By the revenging the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed: * let the sighing of the prisoners come in before thee.
L.8yh: ^78:11^ According to the greatness of thy arm, * take possession of the children of them that have been put to death.
L.8yj: ^78:12^ And render to our neighbours sevenfold in their bosom: * the reproach wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.
L.8yl: ^78:13^ But we thy people, and the sheep of thy pasture, * will give thanks to thee for ever.
L.8yo: ^78:13^ We will shew forth thy praise, * unto generation and generation.
L.8zu: ^79:2^ Qui regis Israël, inténde: * qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph.
L.8zv: ^79:2^ Qui sedes super Chérubim, * manifestáre coram Éphraim, Bénjamin, et Manásse.
L.8zy: ^79:3^ Éxcita poténtiam tuam, et veni, * ut salvos fácias nos.
L.900: ^79:4^ Deus, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
L.901: ^79:5^ Dómine, Deus virtútum, * quoúsque irascéris super oratiónem servi tui?
L.903: ^79:6^ Cibábis nos pane lacrimárum: * et potum dabis nobis in lácrimis in mensúra?
L.905: ^79:7^ Posuísti nos in contradictiónem vicínis nostris: * et inimíci nostri subsannavérunt nos.
L.907: ^79:8^ Deus virtútum, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
L.90a: ^79:9^ Víneam de Ægýpto transtulísti: * ejecísti gentes, et plantásti eam.
L.8z7: ^79:10^ Dux itíneris fuísti in conspéctu ejus: * plantásti radíces ejus, et implévit terram.
L.8z9: ^79:11^ Opéruit montes umbra ejus: * et arbústa ejus cedros Dei.
L.8zb: ^79:12^ Exténdit pálmites suos usque ad mare: * et usque ad flumen propágines ejus.
L.8zd: ^79:13^ Ut quid destruxísti macériam ejus: * et vindémiant eam omnes, qui prætergrediúntur viam?
L.8zf: ^79:14^ Exterminávit eam aper de silva: * et singuláris ferus depástus est eam.
L.8zh: ^79:15^ Deus virtútum, convértere: * réspice de cælo, et vide, et vísita víneam istam.
L.8zk: ^79:16^ Et pérfice eam, quam plantávit déxtera tua: * et super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi.
L.8zl: ^79:17^ Incénsa igni, et suffóssa * ab increpatióne vultus tui períbunt.
L.8zn: ^79:18^ Fiat manus tua super virum déxteræ tuæ: * et super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi.
L.8zq: ^79:19^ Et non discédimus a te, vivificábis nos: * et nomen tuum invocábimus.
L.8zr: ^79:20^ Dómine, Deus virtútum, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
L.8zt: ^79:2^ Give ear, O thou that rulest Israel: * thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep.
L.8zw: ^79:2^ Thou that sittest upon the cherubims, * shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasses.
L.8zx: ^79:3^ Stir up thy might, and come * to save us.
L.8zz: ^79:4^ Convert us, O God: * and shew us thy face, and we shall be saved.
L.902: ^79:5^ O Lord God of hosts, * how long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy servant?
L.904: ^79:6^ How long wilt thou feed us with the bread of tears: * and give us for our drink tears in measure?
L.906: ^79:7^ Thou hast made us to be a contradiction to our neighbours: * and our enemies have scoffed at us.
L.908: ^79:8^ O God of hosts, convert us: * and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.
L.909: ^79:9^ Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt: * thou hast cast out the Gentiles and planted it.
L.8z8: ^79:10^ Thou wast the guide of its journey in its sight: * thou plantedst the roots thereof, and it filled the land.
L.8za: ^79:11^ The shadow of it covered the hills: * and the branches thereof the cedars of God.
L.8zc: ^79:12^ It stretched forth its branches unto the sea, * and its boughs unto the river.
L.8ze: ^79:13^ Why hast thou broken down the hedge thereof, * so that all they who pass by the way do pluck it?
L.8zg: ^79:14^ The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste: * and a singular wild beast hath devoured it.
L.8zi: ^79:15^ Turn again, O God of hosts, * look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard:
L.8zj: ^79:16^ And perfect the same which thy right hand hath planted: * and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.
L.8zm: ^79:17^ Things set on fire and dug down * shall perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.
L.8zo: ^79:18^ Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand: * and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.
L.8zp: ^79:19^ And we depart not from thee, thou shalt quicken us: * and we will call upon thy name.
L.8zs: ^79:20^ O Lord God of hosts, convert us: * and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.
L.xo7: ^Ant.^ Be merciful unto our sins, O Lord.
L.z06: ^Ant.^ O Lord, remember David and all his meekness.
L.scg: ^132:1^ Ecce ^‡^ quam bonum et quam jucúndum, * habitáre fratres in unum:
L.7wu: ^132:2^ Sicut unguéntum in cápite, * quod descéndit in barbam, barbam Aaron,
L.7wt: ^132:2^ Quod descéndit in oram vestiménti ejus: * sicut ros Hermon, qui descéndit in montem Sion.
L.7wx: ^132:3^ Quóniam illic mandávit Dóminus benedictiónem, * et vitam usque in sǽculum.
L.y3d: ^Ant.^ Ecce quam bonum, et quam jucúndum habitáre fratres in unum.
L.scf: ^132:1^ Behold ^‡^ how good and how pleasant it is * for brethren to dwell together in unity:
L.7ws: ^132:2^ Like the precious ointment on the head, * that ran down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron,
L.7wv: ^132:2^ Which ran down to the skirt of his garment: * as the dew of Hermon, which descendeth upon mount Sion.
L.7ww: ^132:3^ For there the Lord hath commanded blessing, * and life for evermore.
L.xoq: ^Ant.^ Behold how good and pleasant it is for brethren to dwell in unity.
L.7xq: ^134:1^ Laudáte nomen Dómini, * laudáte, servi, Dóminum.
L.7xw: ^134:2^ Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
L.7xy: ^134:3^ Laudáte Dóminum, quia bonus Dóminus: * psállite nómini ejus, quóniam suáve.
L.7y1: ^134:4^ Quóniam Jacob elégit sibi Dóminus, * Israël in possessiónem sibi.
L.7y3: ^134:5^ Quia ego cognóvi quod magnus est Dóminus, * et Deus noster præ ómnibus diis.
L.7y5: ^134:6^ Ómnia quæcúmque vóluit, Dóminus fecit in cælo, et in terra, * in mari, et in ómnibus abýssis.
L.7y6: ^134:7^ Edúcens nubes ab extrémo terræ: * fúlgura in plúviam fecit.
L.7y9: ^134:7^ Qui prodúcit ventos de thesáuris suis: * qui percússit primogénita Ægýpti ab hómine usque ad pecus.
L.7ya: ^134:9^ Et misit signa, et prodígia in médio tui, Ægýpte: * in Pharaónem, et in omnes servos ejus.
L.7x7: ^134:10^ Qui percússit gentes multas: * et occídit reges fortes:
L.7x9: ^134:11^ Sehon, regem Amorrhæórum, et Og, regem Basan, * et ómnia regna Chánaan.
L.7xb: ^134:12^ Et dedit terram eórum hereditátem, * hereditátem Israël, pópulo suo.
L.7xc: ^134:13^ Dómine, nomen tuum in ætérnum: * Dómine, memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.
L.7xf: ^134:14^ Quia judicábit Dóminus pópulum suum: * et in servis suis deprecábitur.
L.7xg: ^134:15^ Simulácra géntium argéntum, et aurum, * ópera mánuum hóminum.

L.o62: It is truly fitting and proper, right and profitable to salvation, that we should at all times and in all places give thanks to You, Lord, holy Father, Almighty and everlasting God, through Christ our Lord. For You have promised Him, O faithful and merciful One, as a Saviour for the lost human race; so that His truth might instruct the ignorant, His holiness might sanctify sinners, and His power might strengthen the weak. Since, therefore, the time of His coming is near, and the day of our liberation is dawning, we trust in Your promises and exult with joyous love. And, therefore, with Angels and Archangels, with Thrones and Dominations, and with the whole host of the heavenly army, we sing a hymn to Your glory, saying without ceasing:

L.u27: ^24:10^ Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum ejus et testimónia ejus.
L.u29: ^24:11^ Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.
L.u2a: ^24:12^ Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.
L.u2d: ^24:13^ Ánima ejus in bonis demorábitur: * et semen ejus hereditábit terram.
L.u2e: ^24:14^ Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.
L.u2h: ^24:15^ Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.
L.u2j: ^24:16^ Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.
L.u2l: ^24:17^ Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.
L.u2n: ^24:18^ Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.
L.u2p: ^24:19^ Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.
L.u2s: ^24:20^ Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.
L.u2u: ^24:21^ Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.
L.u2x: ^24:22^ Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.
L.u2r: ^24:1^ To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.
L.u2y: ^24:3^ Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.
L.u31: ^24:4^ Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.
L.u32: ^24:4^ Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.
L.u34: ^24:5^ Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.
L.u36: ^24:6^ Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.
L.u3b: ^24:7^ The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.
L.u38: ^24:7^ According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.
L.u3d: ^24:8^ The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.
L.u3f: ^24:9^ He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.
L.u26: ^24:10^ All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.
L.u28: ^24:11^ For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: * for it is great.
L.u2b: ^24:12^ Who is the man that feareth the Lord? * He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.
L.u2c: ^24:13^ His soul shall dwell in good things: * and his seed shall inherit the land.
L.u2f: ^24:14^ The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: * and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.
L.u2g: ^24:15^ My eyes are ever towards the Lord: * for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.
L.u2i: ^24:16^ Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; * for I am alone and poor.
L.u2k: ^24:17^ The troubles of my heart are multiplied: * deliver me from my necessities.
L.u2m: ^24:18^ See my abjection and my labour; * and forgive me all my sins.
L.u2o: ^24:19^ Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, * and have hated me with an unjust hatred.
L.u2t: ^24:20^ Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: * I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.
L.u2v: ^24:21^ The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: * because I have waited on thee.
L.u2w: ^24:22^ Deliver Israel, O God, * from all his tribulations.
L.my8: Ecce dies véniunt, dicit Dóminus, et suscitábo David germen justum: et regnábit rex, et sápiens erit: et fáciet judícium et justítiam in terra.
L.9pf: ^℟.br.^ Veni ad liberándum nos, * Dómine, Deus virtútum.
L.9ol: ^℟.^ Veni ad liberándum nos, * Dómine, Deus virtútum.
L.9sj: ^℣.^ Osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
L.9l8: ^℟.^ Et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.
L.m5h: Behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a king shall reign, and shall be wise, and shall execute judgement and justice in the earth.
L.9ox: ^℟.br.^ Come to my rescue * O God, Lord of hosts.
L.9ki: ^℟.^ Come to my rescue * O God, Lord of hosts.
L.9t3: ^℣.^ Show us thy face, and we shall be saved.
L.9pw: ^℣.^ And the Gentiles shall fear thy name, O Lord.
L.9k0: ^℟.^ And all the kings of the earth thy glory.
L.nts: In diébus illis salvábitur Juda, et Israël habitábit confidénter: et hoc est nomen, quod vocábunt eum, Dóminus justus noster.
L.9s8: ^℣.^ Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui.
L.o22: In those days shall Juda be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently: and this is the name that they shall call him: the Lord our just one.
L.9pc: ^℟.br.^ Show us, O Lord, * thy mercy.
L.9nr: ^℟.^ Show us, O Lord, * thy mercy.
L.9sy: ^℣.^ Remember us, O Lord, in the favor of thy people.
L.pkz: Prope est ut véniat tempus ejus, et dies ejus non elongabúntur: miserébitur enim Dóminus Jacob, et Israël salvábitur.
L.9qw: ^℣.^ Et glória ejus in te vidébitur.
L.nkt: Her time is near at hand, and her days shall not be prolonged. For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose out of Israel.
L.9pe: ^℟.br.^ The Lord shall arise * upon thee, Jerusalem.
L.9o4: ^℟.^ The Lord shall arise * upon thee, Jerusalem.
L.9pt: ^℣.^ And his glory shall be seen upon thee.
L.9q9: ^℣.^ Come, O Lord, do not be late.
L.9ll: ^℟.^ Forgive the misdeeds of your people.
L.1001: ^Ant.^ We shall go rejoicing into the house of the Lord.
L.7uq: ^122:1^ Ad te levávi óculos meos, * qui hábitas in cælis.
L.7uu: ^122:2^ Ecce, sicut óculi servórum * in mánibus dominórum suórum,
L.7uv: ^122:2^ Sicut óculi ancíllæ in mánibus dóminæ suæ: * ita óculi nostri ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum, donec misereátur nostri.
L.7ux: ^122:3^ Miserére nostri, Dómine, miserére nostri: * quia multum repléti sumus despectióne:
L.7uz: ^122:4^ Quia multum repléta est ánima nostra: * oppróbrium abundántibus, et despéctio supérbis.
L.z8n: ^Ant.^ Qui hábitas in cælis, miserére nobis.
L.zu4: ^Ant.^ Thou who dwellest in the heavens.
L.7ur: ^122:1^ To thee have I lifted up my eyes, * who dwellest in heaven.
L.7ut: ^122:2^ Behold as the eyes of servants * are on the hands of their masters,
L.7us: ^122:2^ As the eyes of the handmaid are on the hands of her mistress: * so are our eyes unto the Lord our God, until he have mercy on us.
L.7uw: ^122:3^ Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: * for we are greatly filled with contempt.
L.7uy: ^122:4^ For our soul is greatly filled: * we are a reproach to the rich, and contempt to the proud.
L.zu3: ^Ant.^ Thou who dwellest in the heavens have mercy upon us.
L.7v1: ^123:1^ Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israël: * nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis,
L.7v2: ^123:2^ Cum exsúrgerent hómines in nos, * forte vivos deglutíssent nos:
L.7v4: ^123:3^ Cum irascerétur furor eórum in nos, * fórsitan aqua absorbuísset nos.
L.7v7: ^123:5^ Torréntem pertransívit ánima nostra: * fórsitan pertransísset ánima nostra aquam intolerábilem.
L.7v8: ^123:6^ Benedíctus Dóminus * qui non dedit nos in captiónem déntibus eórum.
L.7vd: ^123:7^ Ánima nostra sicut passer erépta est * de láqueo venántium:
L.7va: ^123:7^ Láqueus contrítus est, * et nos liberáti sumus.
L.7ve: ^123:8^ Adjutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
L.7v0: ^123:1^ If it had not been that the Lord was with us, let Israel now say: * If it had not been that the Lord was with us,
L.7v3: ^123:2^ When men rose up against us, * perhaps they had swallowed us up alive.
L.7v5: ^123:3^ When their fury was enkindled against us, * perhaps the waters had swallowed us up.
L.7v6: ^123:5^ Our soul hath passed through a torrent: * perhaps our soul had passed through a water insupportable.
L.7v9: ^123:6^ Blessed be the Lord, * who hath not given us to be a prey to their teeth.
L.7vb: ^123:7^ Our soul hath been delivered as a sparrow * out of the snare of the fowlers.
L.7vc: ^123:7^ The snare is broken, * and we are delivered.
L.7vf: ^123:8^ Our help is in the name of the Lord, * who made heaven and earth.
L.z5e: ^Ant.^ Our help is in the name of the Lord.
L.7vg: ^124:1^ Qui confídunt in Dómino, sicut mons Sion: * non commovébitur in ætérnum, qui hábitat in Jerúsalem.
L.7vi: ^124:2^ Montes in circúitu ejus: * et Dóminus in circúitu pópuli sui, ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
L.7vl: ^124:3^ Quia non relínquet Dóminus virgam peccatórum super sortem justórum: * ut non exténdant justi ad iniquitátem manus suas.
L.7vm: ^124:4^ Bénefac, Dómine, bonis, * et rectis corde.
L.7vp: ^124:5^ Declinántes autem in obligatiónes addúcet Dóminus cum operántibus iniquitátem: * pax super Israël.
L.xt2: ^Ant.^ Bénefac Dómine bonis, et rectis corde.
L.7vh: ^124:1^ They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Sion: * he shall not be moved for ever that dwelleth in Jerusalem.
L.7vj: ^124:2^ Mountains are round about it: * so the Lord is round about his people from henceforth now and for ever.
L.7vk: ^124:3^ For the Lord will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the just: * that the just may not stretch forth their hands to iniquity.
L.7vn: ^124:4^ Do good, O Lord, to those that are good, * and to the upright of heart.
L.7vo: ^124:5^ But such as turn aside into bonds, the Lord shall lead out with the workers of iniquity: * peace upon Israel.
L.y0t: ^Ant.^ Do good, O Lord to those that are good, and to the upright of heart.
L.zzr: ^Ant.^ We became like those who are comforted.
L.8ng: ^52:1^ Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.
L.8ni: ^52:2^ Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
L.8nk: ^52:3^ Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
L.8nn: ^52:4^ Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
L.8no: ^52:5^ Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?
L.8nq: ^52:6^ Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
L.8ns: ^52:6^ Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.
L.8nu: ^52:7^ Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Jacob, et lætábitur Israël.
L.8nh: ^52:1^ The fool said in his heart: * There is no God.
L.8nj: ^52:2^ They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.
L.8nl: ^52:3^ God looked down from heaven on the children of men: * to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.
L.8nm: ^52:4^ All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, * there is none that doth good, no not one.
L.8np: ^52:5^ Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, * who eat up my people as they eat bread?
L.8nt: ^52:6^ They have not called upon God: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.
L.8nr: ^52:6^ For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: * they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.
L.8nv: ^52:7^ Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
L.8oy: ^54:2^ Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam, et ne despéxeris deprecatiónem meam: * inténde mihi, et exáudi me.
L.8p0: ^54:3^ Contristátus sum in exercitatióne mea: * et conturbátus sum a voce inimíci, et a tribulatióne peccatóris.
L.8p3: ^54:4^ Quóniam declinavérunt in me iniquitátes: * et in ira molésti erant mihi.
L.8p4: ^54:5^ Cor meum conturbátum est in me: * et formído mortis cécidit super me.
L.8p7: ^54:6^ Timor et tremor venérunt super me: * et contexérunt me ténebræ.
L.8p9: ^54:7^ Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ, * et volábo, et requiéscam?
L.8pa: ^54:8^ Ecce, elongávi fúgiens: * et mansi in solitúdine.
L.8pc: ^54:9^ Exspectábam eum, qui salvum me fecit * a pusillanimitáte spíritus et tempestáte.
L.8nx: ^54:10^ Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum: * quóniam vidi iniquitátem, et contradictiónem in civitáte.
L.8nz: ^54:11^ Die ac nocte circúmdabit eam super muros ejus iníquitas: * et labor in médio ejus, et injustítia.
L.8o1: ^54:12^ Et non defécit de platéis ejus * usúra, et dolus.
L.8o5: ^54:13^ Quóniam si inimícus meus maledixísset mihi, * sustinuíssem útique.
L.8o3: ^54:13^ Et si is, qui óderat me, super me magna locútus fuísset, * abscondíssem me fórsitan ab eo.
L.8o7: ^54:14^ Tu vero, homo unánimis: * dux meus, et notus meus:
L.8o8: ^54:15^ Qui simul mecum dulces capiébas cibos: * in domo Dei ambulávimus cum consénsu.
L.8od: ^54:16^ Véniat mors super illos: * et descéndant in inférnum vivéntes:
L.8oc: ^54:16^ Quóniam nequítiæ in habitáculis eórum: * in médio eórum.
L.8of: ^54:17^ Ego autem ad Deum clamávi: * et Dóminus salvábit me.
L.8oh: ^54:18^ Véspere, et mane, et merídie narrábo et annuntiábo: * et exáudiet vocem meam.
L.8oj: ^54:19^ Rédimet in pace ánimam meam ab his, qui appropínquant mihi: * quóniam inter multos erant mecum.
L.8ok: ^54:20^ Exáudiet Deus, et humiliábit illos, * qui est ante sǽcula.
L.8on: ^54:20^ Non enim est illis commutátio, et non timuérunt Deum: * exténdit manum suam in retribuéndo.
L.8oo: ^54:21^ Contaminavérunt testaméntum ejus, divísi sunt ab ira vultus ejus: * et appropinquávit cor illíus.
L.8or: ^54:22^ Mollíti sunt sermónes ejus super óleum: * et ipsi sunt jácula.
L.8ot: ^54:23^ Jacta super Dóminum curam tuam, et ipse te enútriet: * non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem justo.
L.8ow: ^54:24^ Tu vero, Deus, dedúces eos, * in púteum intéritus.
L.8ox: ^54:24^ Viri sánguinum, et dolósi non dimidiábunt dies suos: * ego autem sperábo in te, Dómine.
L.8oz: ^54:2^ Hear, O God, my prayer, and despise not my supplication: * be attentive to me and hear me.
L.8p1: ^54:3^ I am grieved in my exercise; * and am troubled, at the voice of the enemy, and at the tribulation of the sinner.
L.8p2: ^54:4^ For they have cast iniquities upon me; * and in wrath they were troublesome to me.
L.8p5: ^54:5^ My heart is troubled within me: * and the fear of death is fallen upon me.
L.8p6: ^54:6^ Fear and trembling are come upon me: * and darkness hath covered me.
L.8p8: ^54:7^ And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, * and I will fly and be at rest?
L.8pb: ^54:8^ Lo, I have gone far off flying away; * and I abode in the wilderness.
L.8pd: ^54:9^ I waited for him that hath saved me * from pusillanimity of spirit, and a storm.
L.8nw: ^54:10^ Cast down, O Lord, and divide their tongues; * for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.
L.8ny: ^54:11^ Day and night shall iniquity surround it upon its walls: * and in the midst thereof are labour, and injustice.
L.8o0: ^54:12^ And usury and deceit * have not departed from its streets.
L.8o4: ^54:13^ For if my enemy had reviled me, * I would verily have borne with it.
L.8o2: ^54:13^ And if he that hated me had spoken great things against me, * I would perhaps have hidden myself from him.
L.8o6: ^54:14^ But thou a man of one mind, * my guide, and my familiar.
L.8o9: ^54:15^ Who didst take sweetmeats together with me: * in the house of God we walked with consent.
L.8ob: ^54:16^ Let death come upon them, * and let them go down alive into hell.
L.8oa: ^54:16^ For there is wickedness in their dwellings: * in the midst of them.
L.8oe: ^54:17^ But I have cried to God: * and the Lord will save me.
L.8og: ^54:18^ Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: * and he shall hear my voice.
L.8oi: ^54:19^ He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me: * for among many they were with me.
L.8om: ^54:20^ God shall hear, * and the Eternal shall humble them.
L.8ol: ^54:20^ For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God: * he hath stretched forth his hand to repay.
L.8op: ^54:21^ They have defiled his covenant, they are divided by the wrath of his countenance, * and his heart hath drawn near.
L.8oq: ^54:22^ His words are smoother than oil, * and the same are darts.
L.8os: ^54:23^ Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: * he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever.
L.8ov: ^54:24^ But thou, O God, shalt bring them down * into the pit of destruction.
L.8ou: ^54:24^ Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; * but I will trust in thee, O Lord.
L.yah: ^Ant.^ God bringeth back the captivity of His people.
L.8po: ^55:2^ Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.
L.8pp: ^55:3^ Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.
L.8pr: ^55:4^ Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.
L.8pt: ^55:5^ In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.
L.8pw: ^55:6^ Tota die verba mea exsecrabántur: * advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum.
L.8px: ^55:7^ Inhabitábunt et abscóndent: * ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt.
L.8q0: ^55:8^ Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.
L.8q2: ^55:9^ Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi: * posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
L.8q4: ^55:9^ Sicut et in promissióne tua: * tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum:
L.8pf: ^55:10^ In quacúmque die invocávero te: * ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es.
L.8ph: ^55:11^ In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: * in Deo sperávi, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
L.8pj: ^55:12^ In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, * quæ reddam, laudatiónes tibi.
L.8pm: ^55:13^ Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu: * ut pláceam coram Deo in lúmine vivéntium.
L.8pn: ^55:2^ Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; * all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.
L.8pq: ^55:3^ My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; * for they are many that make war against me.
L.8ps: ^55:4^ From the height of the day I shall fear: * but I will trust in thee.
L.8pu: ^55:5^ In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.
L.8pv: ^55:6^ All the day long they detested my words: * all their thoughts were against me unto evil.
L.8py: ^55:7^ They will dwell and hide themselves: * they will watch my heel.
L.8pz: ^55:8^ As they have waited for my soul, for nothing shalt thou save them: * in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces.
L.8q3: ^55:9^ O God, I have declared to thee my life: * thou hast set my tears in thy sight,
L.8q1: ^55:9^ As also in thy promise. * Then shall my enemies be turned back.
L.8pg: ^55:10^ In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * behold I know thou art my God.
L.8pi: ^55:11^ In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech. * In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me.
L.8pk: ^55:12^ In me, O God, are vows to thee, * which I will pay, praises to thee:
L.8pl: ^55:13^ Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, my feet from falling: * that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living.
L.8qf: ^56:2^ Miserére mei, Deus, miserére mei: * quóniam in te confídit ánima mea.
L.8qd: ^56:2^ Et in umbra alárum tuárum sperábo, * donec tránseat iníquitas.
L.8qg: ^56:3^ Clamábo ad Deum altíssimum: * Deum qui benefécit mihi.
L.8ql: ^56:4^ Misit de cælo, et liberávit me: * dedit in oppróbrium conculcántes me.
L.8qk: ^56:4^ Misit Deus misericórdiam suam, et veritátem suam, * et erípuit ánimam meam de médio catulórum leónum: dormívi conturbátus.
L.8qm: ^56:5^ Fílii hóminum dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: * et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
L.8qp: ^56:6^ Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, * et in omnem terram glória tua.
L.8qr: ^56:7^ Láqueum paravérunt pédibus meis: * et incurvavérunt ánimam meam.
L.8qq: ^56:7^ Fodérunt ante fáciem meam fóveam: * et incidérunt in eam.
L.8qv: ^56:8^ Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam.
L.8qx: ^56:9^ Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
L.8q6: ^56:10^ Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psalmum dicam tibi in géntibus:
L.8q9: ^56:11^ Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad cælos misericórdia tua, * et usque ad nubes véritas tua.
L.8qb: ^56:12^ Exaltáre super cælos, Deus: * et super omnem terram glória tua.
L.z9t: ^Ant.^ Quóniam in te confídit ánima mea.
L.8qe: ^56:2^ Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me: * for my soul trusteth in thee.
L.8qc: ^56:2^ And in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, * until iniquity pass away.
L.8qh: ^56:3^ I will cry to God the most High; * to God who hath done good to me.
L.8qj: ^56:4^ He hath sent from heaven and delivered me: * he hath made them a reproach that trod upon me.
L.8qi: ^56:4^ God hath sent his mercy and his truth, * and he hath delivered my soul from the midst of the young lions. I slept troubled.
L.8qn: ^56:5^ The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows, * and their tongue a sharp sword.
L.8qo: ^56:6^ Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, * and thy glory above all the earth.
L.8qt: ^56:7^ They prepared a snare for my feet; * and they bowed down my soul.
L.8qs: ^56:7^ They dug a pit before my face, * and they are fallen into it.
L.8qu: ^56:8^ My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and rehearse a psalm.
L.8qw: ^56:9^ Arise, O my glory, arise psaltery and harp: * I will arise early.
L.8q7: ^56:10^ I will give praise to thee, O Lord, among the people: * I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations.
L.8q8: ^56:11^ For thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens: * and thy truth unto the clouds.
L.8qa: ^56:12^ Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: * and thy glory above all the earth.
L.y90: ^Ant.^ For my soul trusteth in Thee.
L.8r6: ^57:2^ Si vere útique justítiam loquímini: * recta judicáte, fílii hóminum.
L.8r8: ^57:3^ Étenim in corde iniquitátes operámini: * in terra injustítias manus vestræ concínnant.
L.8r9: ^57:4^ Alienáti sunt peccatóres a vulva, erravérunt ab útero: * locúti sunt falsa.
L.8rb: ^57:5^ Furor illis secúndum similitúdinem serpéntis: * sicut áspidis surdæ, et obturántis aures suas,
L.8rd: ^57:6^ Quæ non exáudiet vocem incantántium: * et venéfici incantántis sapiénter.
L.8rf: ^57:7^ Deus cónteret dentes eórum in ore ipsórum: * molas leónum confrínget Dóminus.
L.8rh: ^57:8^ Ad níhilum devénient tamquam aqua decúrrens: * inténdit arcum suum donec infirméntur.
L.8rk: ^57:9^ Sicut cera, quæ fluit, auferéntur: * supercécidit ignis, et non vidérunt solem.
L.8r0: ^57:10^ Priúsquam intellégerent spinæ vestræ rhamnum: * sicut vivéntes, sic in ira absórbet eos.
L.8r1: ^57:11^ Lætábitur justus cum víderit vindíctam: * manus suas lavábit in sánguine peccatóris.
L.8r4: ^57:12^ Et dicet homo: Si útique est fructus justo: * útique est Deus júdicans eos in terra.
L.8r5: ^57:2^ If in very deed you speak justice: * judge right things, ye sons of men.
L.8r7: ^57:3^ For in your heart you work iniquity: * your hands forge injustice in the earth.
L.8ra: ^57:4^ The wicked are alienated from the womb; they have gone astray from the womb: * they have spoken false things.
L.8rc: ^57:5^ Their madness is according to the likeness of a serpent: * like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ears:
L.8re: ^57:6^ Which will not hear the voice of the charmers; * nor of the wizard that charmeth wisely.
L.8rg: ^57:7^ God shall break in pieces their teeth in their mouth: * the Lord shall break the grinders of the lions.
L.8ri: ^57:8^ They shall come to nothing, like water running down; * he hath bent his bow till they be weakened.
L.8rj: ^57:9^ Like wax that melteth they shall be taken away: * fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun.
L.8qz: ^57:10^ Before your thorns could know the brier; he swalloweth them up, * as alive, in his wrath.
L.8r2: ^57:11^ The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge: * he shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.
L.8r3: ^57:12^ And man shall say: If indeed there be fruit to the just: * there is indeed a God that judgeth them on the earth.
L.yma: ^Ant.^ Judge uprightly O ye sons of men.
L.8rx: ^59:3^ Deus, repulísti nos, et destruxísti nos: * irátus es, et misértus es nobis.
L.8rz: ^59:4^ Commovísti terram, et conturbásti eam: * sana contritiónes ejus, quia commóta est.
L.8s1: ^59:5^ Ostendísti pópulo tuo dura: * potásti nos vino compunctiónis.
L.8s3: ^59:6^ Dedísti metuéntibus te significatiónem: * ut fúgiant a fácie arcus:
L.8s6: ^59:7^ Ut liberéntur dilécti tui: * salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me.
L.8s7: ^59:8^ Deus locútus est in sancto suo: * lætábor, et partíbor Síchimam: et convállem tabernaculórum metíbor.
L.8sc: ^59:9^ Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim fortitúdo cápitis mei.
L.8sb: ^59:9^ Juda rex meus: * Moab olla spei meæ.
L.8rn: ^59:10^ In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ súbditi sunt.
L.8rp: ^59:11^ Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
L.8rr: ^59:12^ Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos? * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
L.8rt: ^59:13^ Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
L.8rv: ^59:14^ In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet tribulántes nos.
L.8ry: ^59:3^ God, thou hast cast us off, and hast destroyed us; * thou hast been angry, and hast had mercy on us.
L.8s0: ^59:4^ Thou hast moved the earth, and hast troubled it: * heal thou the breaches thereof, for it has been moved.
L.8s2: ^59:5^ Thou hast shewn thy people hard things; * thou hast made us drink the wine of sorrow.
L.8s4: ^59:6^ Thou hast given a warning to them that fear thee: * that they may flee from before the bow:
L.8s5: ^59:7^ That thy beloved may be delivered. * Save me with thy right hand, and hear me.
L.8s8: ^59:8^ God hath spoken in his holy place: * I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem; and will mete out the vale of tabernacles.
L.8s9: ^59:9^ Galaad is mine, and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim is the strength of my head.
L.8sa: ^59:9^ Juda is my king: * Moab is the pot of my hope.
L.8ro: ^59:10^ Into Edom will I stretch out my shoe: * to me the foreigners are made subject.
L.8rq: ^59:11^ Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?
L.8rs: ^59:12^ Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go out with our armies?
L.8ru: ^59:13^ Give us help from trouble: * for vain is the salvation of man.
L.8rw: ^59:14^ Through God we shall do mightily: * and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us.
L.xyc: ^Ant.^ Da nobis Dómine auxílium de tribulatióne.
L.y9u: ^Ant.^ Give us help from trouble, O Lord.
L.vzz: ^61:2^ Nonne Deo ^‡^ subjécta erit ánima mea? * ab ipso enim salutáre meum.
L.8t4: ^61:3^ Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus: * suscéptor meus, non movébor ámplius.
L.8t6: ^61:4^ Quoúsque irrúitis in hóminem? * interfícitis univérsi vos: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ?
L.8t8: ^61:5^ Verúmtamen prétium meum cogitavérunt repéllere, cucúrri in siti: * ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant.
L.8ta: ^61:6^ Verúmtamen Deo subjécta esto, ánima mea: * quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea.
L.8tc: ^61:7^ Quia ipse Deus meus, et salvátor meus: * adjútor meus, non emigrábo.
L.8td: ^61:8^ In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea: * Deus auxílii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.
L.8tf: ^61:9^ Speráte in eo omnis congregátio pópuli, effúndite coram illo corda vestra: * Deus adjútor noster in ætérnum.
L.8sx: ^61:10^ Verúmtamen vani fílii hóminum, mendáces fílii hóminum in statéris: * ut decípiant ipsi de vanitáte in idípsum.
L.8sy: ^61:11^ Nolíte speráre in iniquitáte, et rapínas nolíte concupíscere: * divítiæ si áffluant, nolíte cor appónere.
L.8t1: ^61:12^ Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi, quia potéstas Dei est, et tibi, Dómine, misericórdia: * quia tu reddes unicuíque juxta ópera sua.
L.8t2: ^61:2^ Shall not my soul be subject to God? * for from him is my salvation.
L.8t3: ^61:3^ For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my protector, I shall be moved no more.
L.8t5: ^61:4^ How long do you rush in upon a man? * you all kill, as if you were thrusting down a leaning wall, and a tottering fence.
L.8t7: ^61:5^ But they have thought to cast away my price; I ran in thirst: * they blessed with their mouth, but cursed with their heart.
L.8t9: ^61:6^ But be thou, O my soul, subject to God: * for from him is my patience.
L.8tb: ^61:7^ For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my helper, I shall not be moved.
L.8te: ^61:8^ In God is my salvation and my glory: * he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.
L.8tg: ^61:9^ Trust in him, all ye congregation of people: pour out your hearts before him. * God is our helper for ever.
L.8sw: ^61:10^ But vain are the sons of men, the sons of men are liars in the balances: * that by vanity they may together deceive.
L.8sz: ^61:11^ Trust not in iniquity, and cover not robberies: * if riches abound, set not your heart upon them.
L.8t0: ^61:12^ God hath spoken once, these two things have I heard, that power belongeth to God, and mercy to thee, O Lord; * for thou wilt render to every man according to his works.
L.ywr: ^Ant.^ Nonne Deo subjécta erit ánima mea.
L.y12: ^Ant.^ Doth not my soul wait upon God?
L.z10: ^Ant.^ O bless our God ye people.
L.1044: ^Ant.^ Ámplius lava me, Dómine, ab injustítia mea.
L.zzn: ^Ant.^ Wash me yet more, O Lord.
L.zzm: ^Ant.^ Wash me yet more, O Lord, from my iniquity.
L.w0g: ^64:2^ Te decet hymnus, ^‡^ Deus, in Sion: * et tibi reddétur votum in Jerúsalem.
L.zi6: ^Ant.^ Te decet hymnus Deus in Sion.
L.ztj: ^Ant.^ Thou art worthy to be praised.
L.zti: ^Ant.^ Thou art worthy to be praised, O God, in Sion.
L.yqj: ^Ant.^ Lábia mea laudábunt te in vita mea, Deus meus.
L.yub: ^Ant.^ My lips shall praise thee my God, all my life long.
