L.103k: ^Ant.^ Ye heavens of heavens praise the Lord.
L.u5f: ^25:1^ Júdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
L.u5g: ^25:2^ Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
L.u5j: ^25:3^ Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
L.u5l: ^25:4^ Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
L.u5n: ^25:5^ Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
L.u5p: ^25:6^ Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
L.u5r: ^25:7^ Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
L.u5s: ^25:8^ Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
L.u5u: ^25:9^ Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
L.u58: ^25:10^ In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
L.u5b: ^25:11^ Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.
L.u5d: ^25:12^ Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
L.u5e: ^25:1^ Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.
L.u5h: ^25:2^ Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.
L.u5i: ^25:3^ For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.
L.u5k: ^25:4^ I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.
L.u5m: ^25:5^ I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.
L.u5o: ^25:6^ I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:
L.u5q: ^25:7^ That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.
L.u5t: ^25:8^ I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.
L.u5v: ^25:9^ Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: * nor my life with bloody men:
L.u59: ^25:10^ In whose hands are iniquities: * their right hand is filled with gifts.
L.u5a: ^25:11^ But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: * redeem me, and have mercy on me.
L.u5c: ^25:12^ My foot hath stood in the direct way: * in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.
L.yw4: ^Ant.^ Non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
L.yc8: ^Ant.^ He shall not be confounded when he speaks to his enemies in the gate.
L.s3o: ^127:1^ Beáti, ^‡^ omnes, qui timent Dóminum, * qui ámbulant in viis ejus.
L.s3p: ^127:1^ Blessed are all they ^‡^ that fear the Lord: * that walk in his ways.
L.xrp: ^Ant.^ Blessed are all they that fear the Lord.
L.s3r: ^128:1^ Sæpe ^‡^ expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea, * dicat nunc Israël.
L.7vt: ^128:2^ Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea: * étenim non potuérunt mihi.
L.7vu: ^128:3^ Supra dorsum meum fabricavérunt peccatóres: * prolongavérunt iniquitátem suam.
L.7vw: ^128:4^ Dóminus justus concídit cervíces peccatórum: * confundántur et convertántur retrórsum omnes, qui odérunt Sion.
L.7vy: ^128:6^ Fiant sicut fænum tectórum: * quod priúsquam evellátur, exáruit:
L.7w0: ^128:7^ De quo non implévit manum suam qui metit, * et sinum suum qui manípulos cólligit.
L.7w3: ^128:8^ Et non dixérunt qui præteríbant: Benedíctio Dómini super vos: * benedíximus vobis in nómine Dómini.
L.zhj: ^Ant.^ Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea.
L.s3q: ^128:1^ Often ^‡^ have they fought against me from my youth, * let Israel now say.
L.7vs: ^128:2^ Often have they fought against me from my youth: * but they could not prevail over me.
L.7vv: ^128:3^ The wicked have wrought upon my back: * they have lengthened their iniquity.
L.7vx: ^128:4^ The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners: * let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Sion.
L.7vz: ^128:6^ Let them be as grass upon the tops of houses: * which withereth before it be plucked up:
L.7w1: ^128:7^ Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand: * nor he that gathereth sheaves his bosom.
L.7w2: ^128:8^ And they that passed by have not said: The blessing of the Lord be upon you: * we have blessed you in the name of the Lord.
L.z3w: ^Ant.^ Often have they fought against me from my youth.
L.s3s: ^129:1^ De profúndis ^‡^ clamávi ad te, Dómine: * Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:
L.xz0: ^Ant.^ De profúndis clamávi ad te Dómine.
L.s3t: ^129:1^ Out of the depths ^‡^ I have cried to thee, O Lord: * Lord, hear my voice.
L.z5k: ^Ant.^ Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord.
L.7wi: ^130:1^ Dómine, non est exaltátum cor meum: * neque eláti sunt óculi mei.
L.7wk: ^130:1^ Neque ambulávi in magnis: * neque in mirabílibus super me.
L.7wo: ^130:2^ Si non humíliter sentiébam: * sed exaltávi ánimam meam:
L.7wp: ^130:2^ Sicut ablactátus est super matre sua, * ita retribútio in ánima mea.
L.7wr: ^130:3^ Speret Israël in Dómino, * ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
L.7wl: ^130:1^ O Lord, my heart is not exalted: * nor are my eyes lofty.
L.7wj: ^130:1^ Neither have I walked in great matters, * nor in wonderful things above me.
L.7wn: ^130:2^ If I was not humbly minded, * but exalted my soul:
L.7wm: ^130:2^ As a child that is weaned is towards his mother, * so reward in my soul.
L.7wq: ^130:3^ Let Israel hope in the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.
L.ynl: ^Ant.^ Let Israel hope in the Lord.
L.zur: ^Ant.^ Tibi soli peccávi, Dómine, miserére mei.
L.xhl: ^Ant.^ Against thee only have I sinned;
L.xhm: ^Ant.^ Against thee only have I sinned; O Lord, have mercy upon me.
L.wni: ^89:1^ Dómine, ^‡^ refúgium factus es nobis: * a generatióne in generatiónem.
L.z0c: ^Ant.^ O Lord, you have become our refuge.
L.yiz: ^Ant.^ In the morning I shall meditate upon thee.
L.srk: ^15:1^ Cantémus Dómino: ^‡^ glorióse enim magnificátus est, * equum et ascensórem dejécit in mare.
L.srl: ^15:1^ Let us sing ^‡^ to the Lord: for he is gloriously magnified, * the horse and the rider he hath thrown into the sea.
L.yoi: ^Ant.^ Let us sing to the Lord of glory.
L.83b: ^148:1^ Praise ye the Lord ^‡^ from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.
L.z75: ^Ant.^ Praise ye the Lord in his holy places.
L.876: ^22:1^ Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
L.879: ^22:2^ Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
L.87a: ^22:3^ Dedúxit me super sémitas justítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
L.87d: ^22:4^ Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
L.87f: ^22:4^ Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
L.87h: ^22:5^ Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
L.87g: ^22:5^ Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
L.87m: ^22:6^ Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
L.87n: ^22:6^ Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
L.877: ^22:1^ The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.
L.878: ^22:2^ He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.
L.87b: ^22:3^ He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.
L.87c: ^22:4^ For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.
L.87e: ^22:4^ Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.
L.87j: ^22:5^ Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.
L.87i: ^22:5^ Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!
L.87l: ^22:6^ And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.
L.87k: ^22:6^ And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.
L.xrg: ^Ant.^ Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
L.xs3: ^Ant.^ Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.
L.xre: ^Ant.^ Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
L.xrn: ^Ant.^ Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.
L.zvz: ^Ant.^ Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
L.zu9: ^Ant.^ Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.
L.yk9: ^Ant.^ Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
L.100q: ^Ant.^ When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.
L.yqz: ^Ant.^ Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
L.ynr: ^Ant.^ Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.
L.y1z: ^Ant.^ Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
L.z04: ^Ant.^ O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.
L.y1v: ^Ant.^ Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
L.yq3: ^Ant.^ Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.
L.zz4: ^Ant.^ Vitam pétiit * a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decórem imposuísti super eum; posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
L.ybt: ^Ant.^ He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.
L.ydd: ^Ant.^ Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum.
L.ycb: ^Ant.^ He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.
